rule: NEVER execute writes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/BAPI commits/RFM calls with side effects) against P01 or any production system unless the user EXPLICITLY and unambiguously asks for that specific change on that specific day. 'Unblocked', 'executable', 'ready', 'recommended fix' describe STATE — they are NOT authorization to act. Default mode is evaluation / read-only.
why: Session #055 (2026-04-14): when investigating H48, agent listed H45 as 'unblocked, executable'. User reacted with strong pushback: 'NO actualices NADA en PRD!!! SOlo estas evaluando!!!'. The framing of a task as 'executable' was being read as intent-to-execute. Production writes are high-blast-radius and irreversible — misreading state-language as authorization is a class of defect that must be prevented structurally.
how_to_apply: 1) Any language about production fixes (H45/H46/H48 etc.) is EVALUATION only. 2) Before any RFC call that is not RFC_READ_TABLE, ask 'is this a write?'. If yes, stop and confirm in an explicit question to the user. 3) State writes in the FUTURE CONDITIONAL: 'si ejecutas', 'cuando decidas', never 'ejecuto', 'actualizo'. 4) Presentation of a fix (code diff, SQL INSERT, BAPI call) = design deliverable, never auto-implementation. 5) When user says 'ok proceder', verify they mean execute-write vs continue-investigation — if ambiguous, ask. 6) Applies to: P01 always. D01 if change is destructive or affects shared dev state. Quality_gate: any PR or script that writes to P01 must be approved line-by-line in chat before running.

rule: In any custom ABAP program, `CALL TRANSACTION ... USING <bdc> MODE 'E'` (display on error) opens SAPGUI on every BDC error. When the CALL TRANSACTION sits inside a loop driven by `GET <table>` / `LDB_PROCESS` / large `LOOP AT`, the cumulative per-error GUI handshake consumes work-process time proportional to WAN RTT. On slow field-office paths this breaches `rdisp/max_wprun_time` and the dispatcher aborts the caller's LDB fetch with a TIME_OUT whose stack frame points at the LDB's own SELECT, not at the CALL TRANSACTION. Diagnose by checking (a) `CONSTANTS ... VALUE 'E'` declarations, (b) whether the BDC call site is inside a loop body, (c) whether the dump stack bottoms out in standard SAP LDB code (SAPDBSDF, SAPDBADA, etc.). Fix: MODE 'N' (silent) + `MESSAGES INTO <tab>` + post-loop error reporting in the list output. Canonical instance: YTBAE002.abap:27 + :723/:771/:819/:853 (INC-000006906, Claim 54).
why: Session #058 (2026-04-20): INC-000006906 TIME_OUT dump at SAPDBSDF:1983 PUT_BSIS was misdiagnosed for multiple sessions as (a) YBANK set coverage gap (Claim 52, falsified by source grep), (b) empty-range unbounded LDB scan (Claim 53, falsified by user's non-empty GR_SAKNR_OI), (c) data volume (13 BSIS rows, falsified). The dump hint text 'result set too large' and the LDB-code stack frame misdirected every early hypothesis. The real mechanism was only visible after user reproduced same program, same data, same user from HQ LAN in ~2 seconds vs Maputo WAN TIME_OUT. Three-path field reproduction (VPN / Paris / Maputo) isolated network as the decisive axis. Had this rule existed in the brain at the start of the investigation, the YTBAE002.abap:27 MODE 'E' declaration would have been the first code anchor checked, not the last.
how_to_apply: 1) When triaging any TIME_OUT dump in an LDB callback (PUT_BSIS, PUT_BSAS, PUT_BSAD, PUT_BSIK, PUT_BSAK, PUT_BKPF, PUT_COEP, etc.), search the CALLER source for `MODE 'E'` and `CALL TRANSACTION` in parallel. 2) Flag any custom program with `CONSTANTS: <name> TYPE C VALUE 'E'` + at least one `CALL TRANSACTION ... MODE <that_const>` as NETWORK_COUPLED regardless of whether it has dumped yet. 3) Before recommending any other root cause for a field-office TIME_OUT, ask 'does the program open a GUI dialog on BDC error?'. 4) Fix pattern is always the same: MODE 'N' + `MESSAGES INTO tab` + `PERFORM add_to_accumulator USING tab` at each call site + render accumulator post-loop in the list output. YTBAE002's `PROC_RECONCIL_MESS_ADD` + `GT_RECONCIL_MESS` is the reference implementation. 5) Test every new recon / BDC-chained program from a field-office VPN before release; HQ LAN testing is necessary but not sufficient.

rule: When D01 ADT HTTP Basic authentication returns 401 (password locked, expired, or account disabled), do NOT retry the ADT endpoint. Fall back to P01 SNC/SSO + pyrfc + `RPY_PROGRAM_READ` / `RPY_CLASS_READ` / `RPY_FUNCTIONMODULE_READ`. The same source code is visible in both systems because D01 and P01 remain in sync via transport; reading from P01 yields identical bytes for any object that has been promoted. The auth channel differs (SNC/Kerberos vs HTTP Basic), not the content.
why: Session #057 (2026-04-20): JP_LOPEZ's D01 HTTP Basic password was locked during the INC-000006906 source-extraction step. Two options existed: (a) unlock the password and retry ADT, (b) switch to P01 SNC/SSO which was already working. Option (b) took ~3 minutes (import pyrfc, open connection, call RPY_PROGRAM_READ) and produced the same 3,422-line YTBAE002.abap source. Option (a) would have required a password-reset round-trip (~day). The pattern is re-usable: any time D01 ADT 401s, P01 RFC is a same-day alternative for any object that P01 has (which is true for anything released through the D01→TS1→TS3→P01 chain).
how_to_apply: 1) On any D01 ADT HTTP 401 or 'password locked' response, do not retry ADT; switch to pyrfc + P01 SNC/SSO + RPY_PROGRAM_READ and continue. 2) The connection pattern is already documented in `Zagentexecution/sap_data_extraction/rfc_helpers.py`. 3) Write the extracted source to `extracted_code/...` normally; add a manifest note that source_system='P01' so the next agent knows. 4) Only retry D01 ADT if the object in question exists ONLY on D01 (e.g., in-flight customizing not yet transported). 5) Do not spend cycles troubleshooting D01 auth when a same-content alternative exists on P01.

rule: TIME_OUT dumps in SAP-standard LDB callback forms (PUT_BSIS / PUT_BSAS / PUT_BSAD / PUT_BSIK / PUT_BSAK / PUT_BKPF / PUT_COEP / similar) frequently misdirect the analyst. The work-process IS waiting in that SELECT at the moment the dispatcher kills it, but the clock may have been consumed elsewhere: the CALLER's GET-handler doing a CALL TRANSACTION (MODE 'E' handshake over WAN — see `feedback_mode_e_bdc_is_network_coupling_risk`), a COMMIT WORK AND WAIT blocking on replication, an RFC roundtrip to a slow destination, or a synchronous HTTP call from a BAdI. Before filing an 'LDB performance tuning' ticket, inspect what the caller's handler (the GET event, the LDB_PROCESS callback, the NODES include) is doing for each row delivered.
why: Session #058 (2026-04-20): INC-000006906 dump stack bottomed out at SAPDBSDF:1983 PUT_BSIS. For multiple sessions this was read as 'LDB is slow on BSIS / YBANK set is miscoded / empty-range triggers full scan'. All three were wrong. The LDB was entirely fine; the caller (YTBAE002's GET bsis handler) was synchronously opening SAPGUI dialogs on BDC errors via MODE 'E' CALL TRANSACTIONs. The stack frame was an honest pointer to 'where the WP was waiting' but NOT to 'what consumed the time'.
how_to_apply: 1) On any TIME_OUT whose deepest non-standard frame is still SAP-owned (include name starts with SAPDB, SAPL, SAPM, or RFBIBL / RSDB / etc.), pivot IMMEDIATELY to reading the CALLER's code: what program is driving the LDB? What does its GET-handler / callback form do for each row? 2) Specifically check for: `CALL TRANSACTION` (MODE 'E' is worst), `COMMIT WORK AND WAIT`, `CALL FUNCTION ... DESTINATION <remote>`, `CALL TRANSFORMATION`, synchronous BAdI dispatches with `cl_bad_*`. Each of these is a per-row cost multiplier. 3) Compute an order-of-magnitude estimate: if 1 row delivery triggers a 500 ms network round-trip and the LDB delivers 1,000 rows, the WP will exceed a 5-minute cap cleanly. 4) Only after the caller's handler is cleared should LDB tuning (indexes, WHERE pushdown, SELECT * vs INTO TABLE) be considered.

rule: Every substantive agent<->user turn must be captured as a first-class interaction record in brain_v2/interactions/interactions.json with full preserved_full_text. Session-level retros are derived from this layer; they do NOT replace it.
why: Session #055 almost lost the VRSD->E071 pivot knowledge; it survived only because the user asked. Session #058 captured INC-000006906 root cause via turn-level reasoning but only because the agent manually wrote each hypothesis. Violation mode: when a session ends abruptly, tentative hypotheses/corrections/user pushback evaporates — irreversible loss per CP-001. User explicitly directed Session #059: 'we can not compress or lose knowledge we need to efficiently relate every interaction and create more knowledge'.
how_to_apply: Turn types to capture: hypothesis_test, correction, claim_draft, question_asked, question_answered, tool_trace, decision, user_pushback, user_knowledge_contribution, knowledge_preservation_directive. For each: assign INT-<sess>-<turn> ID, 3-axis domain, preserved_full_text (literal quote, NO summary), evidence list (typed refs), links to claims/rules/KUs/incidents/objects. Append to interactions.json immediately — do not batch at session close. Session close flushes _per_session_index, _per_domain_index, _per_object_index reverse indexes.

rule: Every brain node (object, rule, claim, incident, known_unknown, data_quality, superseded, blind_spot, interaction, skill) must carry a non-null domain field using the 3-axis taxonomy {functional, module, process}. At least one axis must be populated. scope='global' is allowed only for truly cross-cutting rules (e.g., core_principles).
why: User directive Session #059: 'Every topic can be assigned to a domain and improve the knowledge or use the knowledge'. Today only objects are domain-tagged (348 occurrences). Rules/claims/KUs/DQs/superseded/skills are untagged — making domain-scoped queries impossible. This is the reason knowledge routing feels ad-hoc: we know WHAT we learned but not WHERE it belongs.
how_to_apply: 3 axes: functional (Treasury/FI/HCM/BCM/Payment/...), module (FI/HCM/TV/MM/BASIS/CTS/...), process (B2R/H2R/P2P/T2R/P2D). Backfill existing 90 rules, 54 claims, 7 incidents, 44 skills. On new node creation, refuse to persist without domain. brain_v2/domains/domains.json is the registry and carries reverse indexes per domain.

rule: At session start, after reading brain_state.json, compute domain activation from the user's first substantive prompt using domains.json session_activation_hints. Auto-load knowledge_docs + skills + open KUs/DQs + companions for the activated domain(s). Log the activation decision as an interaction (type=decision).
why: Without this, the agent rediscovers which skills/docs/KUs are relevant on every session — wastes cache tokens, misses links, and causes the 'context loaded but not used' failure mode (the problem Layer 11 incidents solved at its own granularity, now solved at domain granularity). User directive Session #059 anchors domains as the routing substrate.
how_to_apply: 1. Scan user first prompt for keywords in domains.json._session_activation_hints regex map. 2. Produce ordered list of activated domains. 3. For each: read its knowledge_docs, note its skills, enumerate open KUs/DQs, reference its companions. 4. Announce 'Active domain(s)' in text before first tool call. 5. Persist the activation as INT-<sess>-000 interaction. 6. If no match: log as blind_spot candidate 'unclassified_session_scope'.

rule: When migrating an XML payment format to ISO 20022 structured address, default to Hybrid (TwnNm+Ctry mandatory + AdrLine fallback) unless each specific bank spec demands fully-structured. Never assume all banks have identical strictness.
why: CBPR+ Nov 2026 mandate permits Hybrid (structured + AdrLine coexist) as a valid compliance state. The handoff doc for UNESCO session #62 explicitly confirms TwnNm+Ctry are the only hard-required fields. Defaulting to Hybrid preserves rollback safety and accommodates vendor master DQ gaps (UNESCO 5% missing STREET, 68% missing HOUSE_NUM1 but 99.995% have CITY1+COUNTRY). Going to fully-structured by default wastes effort on vendor master cleanup that may not be required by all banks.
how_to_apply: Before committing to 'only structured' scope, (1) collect each bank's written spec for structured-address strictness, (2) measure vendor master DQ per field to know the cost of fully-structured, (3) default to Hybrid per bank unless bank spec is explicit. Re-evaluate stricter modes post-go-live on a per-bank basis.

rule: Structured-address migration in SAP DMEE has THREE distinct technical patterns by XML party, not one. Do not confuse them: (1) Cdtr address is SAP-auto-populated via FPAYHX Z-fields bound to vendor master LFA1+ADRC — DMEE tree config only, no ABAP needed. (2) Dbtr address is NOT in FPAYHX/FPAYH — requires ABAP user exit registered in OBPM4 Event 05 that reads T001→ADRC and writes FPAYHX-ZREF01..ZREF05 (NOT FPAYH-REF). (3) UltmtCdtr (alternative payee) may require a data source decision (vendor master / Z-table / separate user exit) per bank/format.
why: UNESCO handoff doc §5 conflated the three patterns causing scope confusion in session #62. Dbtr requires a new FM while Cdtr does not. Mistaking the two leads to either unnecessary ABAP or missing ABAP — both are schedule-breakers for a Nov 2026 deadline.
how_to_apply: When scoping a structured-address change, decompose per XML party (Dbtr/Cdtr/UltmtCdtr/CdtrAgt) and apply the correct pattern to each. Cdtr = tree-only. Dbtr = tree + user exit + OBPM4 registration. UltmtCdtr = decision-first, spec-second, code-third.

rule: A user exit FM for DMEE can be registered in multiple PMW formats via OBPM4 simultaneously. Write once, reuse across formats. Avoid per-format FM duplication.
why: Handoff doc recommends this; UNESCO has 3 target DMEE trees (SEPA_CT_UNES, CITI DC_V3_01, CGI_XML_CT_UNESCO) that all need the same Dbtr address enrichment logic. Building 3 FMs triples maintenance and drift risk.
how_to_apply: When creating Z_DMEE_UNESCO_DEBTOR_ADDR or similar FMs, register it in OBPM4 for all needed PMW formats using Event 05. Centralize logic; format-specific tweaks go behind IF statements keyed on format name, not in separate FMs.

rule: When designing a new ISO 20022 / pain.001 DMEE tree (or version) that needs structured address, source the structured nodes from FPAYHX-REF01/REF02/REF06 using SAP-std byte offsets — do NOT design a custom UNESCO BAdI for address. The SAP-std GENERIC class (CL_IDFI_CGI_CALL05_GENERIC) populates these REF buffers from ADRC at every Event 05 call: REF01[0..60]=street, [60..80]=building, [80..90]=post_code1, [90..100]=region, [100..110]=house_num1; REF02 has Cdtr equivalents; REF06[0..40]=city. Country classes (FR/DE/IT/GB) only ADD REF14 country-specific data, never override the address layout.
why: Phase 0/1 expert re-evaluation discovered that SEPA structured address was thought to require new ABAP, but the SAP-std generic class already does the address-to-REF mapping universally. Avoiding custom address BAdI keeps the change surgical (config-only for SEPA) and aligned with SAP-supported pattern.
how_to_apply: (1) For a new pain.001 tree: register a payment-medium FM (typically FI_PAYMEDIUM_DMEE_CGI_05) for Event 05 in TFPM042FB. (2) Add DMEE nodes for StrtNm/BldgNb/PstCd/TwnNm/Ctry sourced from FPAYHX-REF01 with the byte-offset layout above (use MP_SC_FLD=REF01 + MP_OFFSET + appropriate length). (3) Verify in DMEE Tx Test mode with a sample FPAYHX payload before deploying to D01.

rule: When classifying any object as ACTIVE or DEAD, the verdict MUST be anchored on P01 runtime evidence — NEVER on D01 existence alone. D01 may carry stale/experimental code that is not active in production. Active = exists in P01 + has a runtime hook (DMEE_TREE_HEAD active version, TFPM042FB Event 05 registration, MP_EXIT_FUNC in DMEE_TREE_NODE, ENHO impl active for BAdI dispatch, T042Z payment method routing).
why: Drift between D01 and P01 is normal in legacy SAP shops. Trust D01 only as a deployment target, not as truth. Multiple times during Phase 0 we found objects in one but not the other — the right question is always: does P01 use it today?
how_to_apply: Before declaring an object active or dead: (1) check P01 DMEE_TREE_HEAD for trees, (2) check TFPM042FB for FM Event 05 registrations, (3) check DMEE_TREE_NODE.MP_EXIT_FUNC for node-level FM hooks, (4) check ENHHEADER/SXS_ATTR for ENHO impl active flag, (5) check T042Z for routing. If any layer confirms P01 use, mark ACTIVE. If no P01 layer references it, mark DEAD or NEEDS_VERIFY (do NOT mark ACTIVE based on D01 presence).
examples: Z_DMEE_EXIT_TAX_NUMBER initially flagged D01-only (no source FT include in P01) -> wrong verdict. Re-check via MP_EXIT_FUNC showed FM IS active in P01 CITI tree. The ====FT include is just D01 leftover; the FM proper exists in P01 via different include.

YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_DE class is P01-only; we mark it ACTIVE because Y_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_COUNTRIES_DE ENHO + the class source from P01 prove dispatch. D01 absence is what triggers the retrofit transport need.

rule: When a question, blocker, or 'deferred' item gets RESOLVED, propagate the resolution to every companion section that previously cited it. Do NOT rely on adding a new section alone — search the entire companion (and any upstream knowledge docs) for stale phrases like 'deferred to V002', 'still open', 'NO change', 'pending TRM', 'awaiting input' bound to the resolved Q-id, and update them in the same commit.
why: Session #62 commit a6b2895 added brain claim 99 (Q3 UltmtCdtr Worldlink RESOLVED system-driven) and added a new '🧪 Simulator (100%)' tab + Sections 13/14 to CONCLUSIONS_TABLES. But the companion's Scope tab kept 'UltmtCdtr Worldlink (Q3) — DEFERRED to V002' in the OUT-OF-SCOPE list, the Change Strategy tab kept 'UltmtCdtr Worldlink (Q3) → V002 deferred' in decisions-baked, and the e2e_flow Critical-decisions table also kept 'UltmtCdtr Worldlink → V002 deferred · Q3 still open, defer'. The CGI tree row stayed 'NO tree edits' even though the canonical plan (line 222) said 'Fix CdtrAgt only'. Result: Session #63 read the companion and found three live contradictions — one between the companion Scope and Strategy tabs internally, and one between the companion and the canonical plan. Required a full re-alignment pass that should have been one edit at the original commit. This violates CLAUDE.md cross-reference rule ('grep for the entity name across ALL companions and reports').
how_to_apply:
Mandatory checklist whenever a Q-id, gap, or deferred item resolves:
1. `grep -rn '<Q-id>\|<gap-id>\|<topic>' companions/ knowledge/` — list every match
2. For each match: classify as (a) historical record (keep, mark with date), (b) decision-baked / current-state claim (UPDATE), (c) OUT-OF-SCOPE list (REMOVE or MOVE to in-scope)
3. If the resolution changes the change scope (e.g. Q3 unifies into V001), update Scope rows + total counters + per-tree strategy table in the same commit
4. Add the resolution as evidence_for in the brain claim BEFORE editing companions, so the cite is concrete
5. Do NOT close the session until grep returns zero stale references for that Q-id
6. Single-tab updates without cross-section sweep are anti-pattern — companion users navigate by tab and will read the stale tab as authoritative
cp_link_reason: Knowledge over velocity — adding a new tab without sweeping stale tabs is the velocity-over-trazabilidad failure mode CP-001 names directly. Future sessions read whichever tab they hit first; if that tab is stale, every downstream decision is built on the wrong premise.

rule: Every assertion written into a companion (or any user-facing artifact: report, plan, slide deck, email draft) must be anchored to a brain artifact — claim id, object annotation, KU, incident, falsification, plan section path:line, or process mining file path. If the assertion has no brain anchor, the agent must FIRST add it to the brain (as a TIER-classified claim or KU) and THEN use the brain id as the cite. TIER_3 inferred assertions must be visibly flagged in the companion text (e.g. '[INFERRED]', italic '~', or a footnote) so the reader knows the basis.
why: User directive 2026-04-29 (Session #63) after Overview-tab enrichment landed: 'All the improvement that we will do should be based on our Brain. And validated by our AGI.' Operationalizes CP-003 (Precision, evidence, facts) for the companion-editing path. Until now, CP-003 governed individual claims — but companion paragraphs wrap many micro-assertions in prose, and those drift unanchored. The Overview enrichment in Session #63 included assertions that were correct but unanchored ('GBP, KRW, NGN, INR' currency examples for CGI tree, 'UIS uses CITI for local payments' from user-testimony only) — which under this rule would either need explicit anchors inline or a brain claim added FIRST. The failure mode this rule prevents: companion text that is plausible and authoritative-looking but cannot be falsified, audited, or chained back to evidence by the next agent.
how_to_apply:
Before saving any companion edit:
1. Re-read the diff. For each factual assertion (number, name, mechanism, who-uses-what), ask: is there a brain anchor for this?
2. If YES → cite inline. Format: '(claim 99)', '(plan §Per-tree design L550)', '(brain object YTBAE002)', '(process_mining_real_tree_per_payment.json)'. Citing in a footnote or 'sources' block is acceptable for prose-heavy sections; inline is required for tables and decision artifacts.
3. If NO and the assertion is verifiable → add a TIER_1 claim or TIER_2 empirical claim to brain FIRST (or a KU if needs more research). Then cite the new id.
4. If NO and the assertion is genuinely inferred → flag with [INFERRED] tag in the companion text + add a TIER_3 claim with the inference chain documented (so it's falsifiable later).
5. If NO and the assertion is irrelevant decoration → DELETE it. Companion is not a place for vibes.
6. After the edit, re-run brain rebuild + grep companion for unanchored numbers/names. Ship only when zero unanchored facts remain.
cp_link_reason: Direct operationalization of CP-003 'Precision, evidence, facts' for the companion-editing path. CP-003 already mandates tier+evidence for individual claims; this rule extends that mandate to every prose assertion in user-facing artifacts. Without it, companions drift from anchored knowledge to plausibility narrative — exactly the failure CP-003 names ('Plausibility es indistinguible de hallucination para el usuario').

rule: When an originally-framed external dependency (bank TRM, third-party SME, vendor support, customer interview) has its underlying question answerable from system-internal evidence (brain claims, extracted source code, Gold DB tables, process-mining data, deterministic simulators), CLOSE the external dependency and ANSWER from system. External communications become coordination/courtesy/notification — not gating prerequisites for design or scope decisions.
why: Three concrete instances at UNESCO BCM Structured Address (Sessions #62-63) where this pattern paid off: (1) Q3 (Worldlink UltmtCdtr data source) — originally framed "needs Citi TRM + DBS input"; resolved 2026-04-29 via DMEE_TREE_NODE analysis (claim 99). 7 source fields confirmed from system. No external input needed. (2) A5 (separate PMW per entity) — originally "check FBZP during Phase 1"; closed 2026-04-30 via Gold DB PRAGMA on T042Z (claim 103). T042Z has no ZBUKR column, routing is uniform. (3) A1 (per-bank strictness) — originally "9 questions to each TRM as Phase 1 prerequisite"; closed 2026-04-30 by combining simulator 794/794 PASS on .03+.09 + V001 Fully-Structured commitment. CBPR+ minimum is Hybrid; shipping Fully-Structured automatically satisfies any bank strictness. The external pattern would have lost 2-4 weeks of bank-response wait time per question; system-internal answers were instant. The failure mode this rule prevents: agents treating external SME/bank input as the default channel and waiting for replies on questions that were already answerable from extracted data.
how_to_apply: Whenever a question is framed as "needs external X input": (1) Decompose: what system-internal evidence (brain claims, code, Gold DB, simulator, process-mining) could answer this? (2) Run the system query first. (3) If system answers definitively → CLOSE the external dependency, mark the question RESOLVED system-driven, cite the evidence, downgrade external comms to coordination only. (4) If system answers partially → use system answer as the design assumption + use external comms only to falsify if needed. (5) If system cannot answer → external comms remains gating, but only on the residual question, not on the original full scope. Do NOT default to "ask the SME" without first checking what the brain already knows.
cp_link_reason: Direct application of CP-002 "Preserve first, context is cheap" — the brain already preserves the answer; defaulting to external SME bypasses preserved knowledge. Also reinforces CP-003 (precision/evidence) — system queries return cite-able answers; SME responses often return opinions without source citations.

rule: When writing or editing companion sections (companions/*.html or any human-facing knowledge artifact rendered for stakeholders), apply the 'friendly explanation' pattern: why-before-what intro, analogies, highlighted callouts, plain-English read-backs, end with 'what this means for [project]' anchor. Do NOT drop tables/screenshots on the reader cold without surrounding narrative.
why: Session 2026-04-30 DME submenu added under Overview in companions/BCM_StructuredAddressChange.html. Initial draft was tag-style: dense tables and 'tagged' screenshot captions with no surrounding prose. User explicit pushback mid-session: 'Can we do a more user friendly explanation in the sections are very short explanations'. Companions are read by M_SPRONK (functional), N_MENARD (technical), Pablo (lead), F. Spezzano (parallel work) and any future agent or SME joining the project. Tables alone cause readers to bounce; narrative builds the mental models that let readers reuse the document months later. The corrective rewrite added 138 lines of prose (3782->3920) using analogies (Mail Merge, Lego pieces, three locks in series, 5-act play, library catalog), highlighted insight callouts, and per-section 'what V001 changes here' anchors. The user signed off ('ok'). Failure mode this rule prevents: terse-tag style content that is information-dense but onboarding-hostile.
how_to_apply: 10-point checklist for every human-facing companion or knowledge section. (1) Open with 'Why this exists' before 'What it is' - frame the problem before the solution. (2) Use analogies that map SAP concepts to everyday domains - Mail Merge for DMEE+PMW, Lego pieces for node types, locks in series for FBZP layers, 5-act play for F110 runtime, library catalog for OBPM1. (3) Highlighted callout boxes (green-bordered or equivalent visual treatment) for traps, surprises, and key insights - pulls reader's eye to high-leverage facts. (4) Walk-throughs with concrete step-by-step before reference tables. (5) Plain-English read-back paragraphs after every technical block ('read this in plain English: F110 picks ... posts ... hands off to ...'). (6) Decode acronyms first time used (FDTA = Fi Data medium Transfer Administration). (7) Concrete examples from real data when possible (vendor 200135, SocGen, Citi, FB00, /SEPA_CT_UNES). (8) End each section with 'What [V001 / this project / current work] does at this layer' anchor connecting back to the project's core narrative. (9) Keep existing tables and screenshots - narrative wraps around, never replaces them. They are visual anchors that scan well; prose teaches. (10) 'If you only read one X, read this' prioritisation markers for the high-leverage rows in long tables. APPLIES TO: all companion edits, all knowledge/ docs aimed at humans (not raw data dumps). DOES NOT APPLY TO: agent-internal artifacts (brain JSON, CSV exports, raw data files, machine-readable schemas) which stay terse by design.
cp_link_reason: CP-001 'Knowledge over velocity' applies here: it is faster to ship a tag-style table dump, but the resulting companion has near-zero teaching value. Future agents and stakeholders cannot rebuild the mental model from terse tags alone, so they re-derive the knowledge from scratch each time, paying the velocity cost twice. Investing 138 lines of narrative once amortises across every future read.

rule: Do NOT use dark mode (dark backgrounds with light text) in companion HTML pages. Default to a light theme: white or near-white background, dark text, restrained accent colors. This applies to all NEW companion sections and to retro-fits when sections are touched. Existing dark-themed companions are NOT auto-migrated, but every new section/companion must be light.
why: User directive 2026-04-30 right after sign-off on the friendly-explanation rule: 'add additionally that we should not use Dark mode'. The existing companions/BCM_StructuredAddressChange.html uses a dark theme (background #0c1926, text #d6e5f5, accents #1abc9c) inherited from the original Session #62 build. Several stakeholder readers (M_SPRONK, F. Spezzano, external SMEs) read companions printed, projected, or in shared-screen settings where dark themes wash out, lose contrast, and are harder to print. Light mode is the safer default for stakeholder-facing artifacts. Failure mode this rule prevents: agents continuing the dark-mode pattern by inertia when extending existing companions or starting new ones.
how_to_apply: When creating or extending companion HTML: (1) Default body/container backgrounds to white (#ffffff) or near-white (#fafbfc, #f5f7fa). (2) Body text dark (#1a2332, #2c3e50, #333). (3) Accent colors restrained - prefer SAP-style blues (#0070f2, #1976d2) or muted teals over neon. (4) Tables: light header row (#e8eef4 or #f0f4f8), white body rows with subtle alternating zebra (#fafbfc). (5) Code/pre blocks: light grey (#f5f5f5 or #f8f9fa) with dark text. (6) Callout/insight boxes: pastel-tinted backgrounds (#e8f5e9 green, #fff3e0 amber, #e3f2fd blue) with dark text. (7) Borders subtle (#dde3eb, #e0e0e0). When editing an existing dark-mode companion, do NOT migrate the whole file unless explicitly asked - add new sections in light mode and flag the inconsistency in the PR/commit message. EXCEPTION: if the user explicitly requests dark mode for a specific artifact, honor it and note the override.

rule: For any UNESCO SAP change involving D01->P01 transport path: P01 is the canonical source of truth for live config. D01 may carry uncommitted draft versions (verified 2x cohabitation pattern on /SEPA_CT_UNES, /CGI_XML_CT_UNESCO, /CGI_XML_CT_UNESCO_1 - D01 has exactly 2x the node count of P01). Therefore: NO change is applied to D01 until D01 has been byte-aligned with P01 (Step-0 RETROFIT). The sequence is invariant: (1) P01 source-of-truth snapshot, (2) D01 retrofit (purge or promote draft cohabitation), (3) D01 verification = P01 by node count + by checksum, (4) ONLY THEN apply the planned change in D01, (5) test then transport to V01 then P01.
why: User directive 2026-04-30 (Session #63) after surfacing the 2x drift visualisation in companion Current Solution tab. Brain claim 108 documents the evidence: 2x cohabitation is exact on all custom UNESCO trees while SAP-std trees match 1:1. This is NOT accumulated drift - it is unfinished WIP versions cohabiting with the P01-mirror in D01. Failure modes if rule is violated: (a) V001 change matrix rows targeting P01 NODE_IDs will land on the wrong layer in D01 (the draft sibling) and silently corrupt; (b) V001 transport packing in D01 may pick up draft nodes that were never meant to ship; (c) developer confusion when D01 view shows nodes M_SPRONK never confirmed; (d) Phase 4 UAT will diverge from production baseline. None of these failure modes are detectable by the simulator (which works on P01 data) or by XSD validation (which only checks schema).
how_to_apply: Mandatory pre-flight check before any planned change: (1) Extract current P01 state of target object (RFC RPY_*_READ / RFC_READ_TABLE) - record byte hash. (2) Extract current D01 state - record byte hash. (3) If hashes match - proceed with planned change in D01. (4) If hashes differ - STOP. Triage divergence: per-row classify as P01-only (retrofit DOWN), D01-only-draft (purge OR promote), content-different (reconcile via separate transport). (5) Execute D01-RETROFIT-N transport bringing D01 to byte-equality with P01. (6) Re-run hash check - must match. (7) Apply planned change. (8) Verify the change is the ONLY delta in the new transport (E071 inspection). For Phase 2 V001 specifically: D01-RETROFIT-01 scope is full byte-alignment of all 4 in-scope trees plus the 5 P01-only ABAP objects (Finding I). After retrofit, the V001 change matrix (27 rows) is applied. NO row is applied before retrofit completes.
cp_link_reason: CP-003 precision/evidence/facts: cannot make a precise change against an imprecise baseline. D01 with 2x cohabitation is an imprecise baseline. Also CP-001: skipping retrofit feels faster but loses byte-level traceability.

rule: Before claiming a SAP business-rule field is enforced (validation/required/auto-derived), audit ALL 5 layers: (1) SAP-std F4-help/required-flag at field level, (2) GGB0 validation rules (BOOLCLASS-scoped), (3) GGB1 substitution rules, (4) custom Z-code (form pool / BAdI), (5) master-data discipline. Document each layer's verdict separately. A green at one layer does NOT imply enforcement; F4-help only validates entered values, it does not require entry.
why: Session #63 LZBKZ-PPC audit: T015L has 73 codes for 9 PPC countries (looks like enforcement infrastructure exists), but full 5-layer audit revealed ZERO upstream validation. AP clerk can post invoices without LZBKZ to PPC-country vendors → F110 emits empty PPC tag → bank rejects. Without disciplined per-layer audit, the surface presence of master config (T015L populated) plus runtime infrastructure (YTFI_PPC_*, BAdI dispatch) created a false sense that the field was enforced. Same pattern likely exists for other country-bank-required fields (e.g., IBAN for PL, tax ID for BR, withholding for various jurisdictions).
how_to_apply: When asked 'is field X enforced?' or before stating 'SAP requires Y at posting': run the 5-layer audit query — F4 (T-code SE11 → element check), GGB0 (Gold DB GB931 / SE38 RGUGBR00), GGB1 (Gold DB GB922 SUBSFIELD='X'), Z-code (grep YRGGBS00 + relevant BAdIs/exits), vendor master (LFB1/LFBK Z-fields + LFA1 mandatory flags). Report per-layer verdict. If <2 layers enforce → flag as GAP and propose hard-stop validation step in GGB0 as primary fix. Caveat: claim 39 — F110 BAPI_ACC_DOCUMENT_POST may bypass callpoints; verify callpoint 2 fires for BAPI postings before relying on GGB0 alone.
cp_link_reason: Precision + evidence: claiming enforcement without per-layer audit is opinion masquerading as fact. The 5-layer audit forces evidence per layer, anchored in checkable Gold DB queries + extracted source greps.

rule: In operator-facing artifacts (companion HTML, plan documents, design specs, training material, dry-run procedures), address DMEE tree nodes by their full path (Document > CstmrCdtTrfInitn > PmtInf > Dbtr > PstlAdr > StrtNm), NOT by their internal NODE_ID (e.g. N_4754354180). NODE_IDs are unique technical identifiers but are invisible to operators in the tx DMEE tree pane - operators navigate the tree by clicking through indentation levels, and the path they click is what unambiguously identifies a node. NODE_IDs are reserved for technical reference channels (v001_change_matrix.csv 'technical reference' columns, RFC verification SQL, brain claim evidence anchors). Same TECH_NAME values repeat at multiple levels in any DMEE tree (e.g. Nm appears under InitgPty/Dbtr/Cdtr/UltmtCdtr/UltmtDbtr; PstlAdr appears under Dbtr at PmtInf level AND under Cdtr at CdtTrfTxInf level), so addressing by TECH_NAME alone is ambiguous - always include the parent path in operator-facing wording.
why: Session #65 user pushback (2026-04-30) on companion BCM_StructuredAddressChange.html: the bridge mapping section used 'Cdtr/PstlAdr (parent N_4754354180)' as the addressing convention. User explicit corrections: 'screen is not correctly map, we have multiple levels and names', 'we have a total desconection between the UI way of configurate levels and the XML emited'. Root cause: NODE_IDs are an artifact of the DMEE_TREE_NODE table schema, not part of the operator's mental model. When the operator opens tx DMEE Display Format Tree, they see indentation + TECH_NAME labels - never NODE_IDs. Using NODE_IDs in operator-facing artifacts forces a translation step that breaks the connection between UI configuration and XML output. Failure mode this rule prevents: future agents (or this agent in future sessions) reverting to NODE_ID addressing when documenting V001 / V002 / future bank-format changes, making the artifacts unusable for operators.
how_to_apply: When writing or editing any DMEE-related operator-facing artifact: 1. Address each node by its full path from Document down to the leaf, e.g. Document > CstmrCdtTrfInitn > PmtInf > Dbtr > PstlAdr. 2. If multiple instances of the same TECH_NAME exist in the same tree, ALWAYS distinguish them by path (PmtInf > Dbtr > PstlAdr versus CdtTrfTxInf > Cdtr > PstlAdr). 3. NODE_IDs are PERMITTED only in technical-reference columns of CSVs/JSONs (e.g. v001_change_matrix.csv) and in brain claim evidence anchors where they pin RFC-extracted data to specific rows. 4. When showing UI <-> XML mappings, render the UI side as indented hierarchy with explicit path breadcrumbs and the XML side with matching nesting depth. The 1:1 visual alignment is the bridge. 5. The hierarchy collapse pattern (95-node tree -> 2 INSERT targets at level 5/6) is the operator's mental model - use it in any new DMEE design content. 6. Brain anchors: claim 117 (hierarchy collapse), claim 118 (UI=XML 1:1), claim 119 (path disambiguation), claim 120 (empty-suppress).

rule: When documenting a SAP migration project in the companion HTML (or any operator-facing artifact), split content into two clearly-distinct zones: (1) Current Solution / V000 baseline — how the system is wired and behaving today, organized per object (per tree, per program, per workflow), and (2) Change Strategy / V001 changes — the specific deltas the project introduces, also organized per object. Cross-reference between the two zones with explicit links so a reader looking at a V001 delta can jump to the V000 baseline for that same object, and vice versa. Do NOT mix V000 baseline content with V001 delta content in the same section — the cognitive cost of switching context line-by-line is high, and operators reading for one specific object end up scrolling through unrelated other-object material.
why: Session #65 user pushback on the DMEE Configuration tab: 'maybe some information should be moved to Current Solution and only keep the specific changes here'. Root cause: the original tab mixed V000 baseline material (tree structure ASCII, 6-tabs settings, hierarchy stratification, screenshots of the today-state) with V001 delta material (per-target INSERTs, Step A/B/C walkthroughs, code-change indicators). Operators reading for ONE tree had to scroll through both kinds of content for SEPA (used as worked example) before reaching their tree's specific deltas. The cleaner split: V000 baseline content lives in Current Solution per-tree; V001 delta content lives in Change Strategy → DMEE Configuration per-tree sub-tabs. Each tree's V001 sub-tab carries a back-link to its V000 baseline; each V000 baseline carries a forward-link to its V001 deltas. Result: operators reading one tree end-to-end open just two locations (V000 + V001) instead of scrolling through all-tree concept material first.
how_to_apply: When creating or restructuring a companion that documents a SAP migration project: 1. Identify the units of work (trees, programs, workflows, configurations). 2. Allocate two zones: Current Solution (V000 baseline per unit) + Change Strategy (V001 deltas per unit). 3. For each unit, write a self-contained section in BOTH zones: V000 section describes how it works today;    V001 section describes the specific changes. 4. Add explicit cross-references at the top of each section pointing to its counterpart in the other zone. 5. Cross-tree concepts (rules that apply to all units — e.g. 'UI indentation = XML nesting depth') live in    the V001 zone foundations sub-tab OR in a shared concept page; not duplicated per unit. 6. When a V001 change explicitly references a V000 element (e.g. 'INSERT child under existing PstlAdr'),    the V001 prose says 'see Current Solution → Tree X for the V000 baseline of PstlAdr'. 7. Sub-tabs in the sidebar (one per unit) make navigation explicit — the operator clicks the unit they care    about and reads end-to-end. APPLIES TO: companion HTML pages, multi-page knowledge artifacts, project plans. DOES NOT APPLY TO: brain JSON, raw matrix CSVs, or any non-stakeholder-facing artifact.

cp_link_reason: CP-001 'Knowledge over velocity': mixing V000 baseline with V001 changes is faster to write because there's no second zone to maintain, but operators pay the cognitive cost on every read. Splitting once (zones + cross-references) amortises across every operator who reads the companion thereafter. why: INC-000005638 (2026-05-01): Without this rule, the analyst would burn cycles checking ZXFMYU22 10-digit hard link, ZXFMDTU02 hardcodes, ZXFMCU17 tolerance cap, and ZXM06U22 release strategy - all of which pass clean. The actual root cause is at the AVC pool / biennium-close-out process layer, not in custom code. UNESCO's biennium pattern is highly regular (196EAR4037 through 4043 covering 2014-2015 through 2026-2027 in 2-year increments) and reading PROJ.POST1 reveals it in seconds. The detector inc5638_avc_fipex_deficit.py confirms 2,153 of 2,708 (79.5pct) donor (FUND, FUNDSCTR) buckets fit this class signature - this is not a per-incident defect, it is a recurring class.
how_to_apply: 1. Confirm the user's reported PO/SES touches a fund. 2. Read funds.TYPE (must be 101-112 for donor scope). 3. Read proj.POST1 - look for biennium tag like '(YYYY-YYYY)'. 4. If biennium found, check whether successor fund exists: SELECT * FROM funds WHERE FINCODE = predecessor_FINCODE_with_last_digit_incremented. 5. If successor exists AND its proj.POST1 names the new biennium, you are likely in INC-000005638 class. 6. Confirm via Zagentexecution/quality_checks/inc5638_avc_fipex_deficit.py. 7. Recommend FMAVCREINIT and biennium-close-out review. 8. DO NOT spend cycles on ZXFMYU22 hardcodes / FMDERIVE / tolerance caps unless the predecessor fund is NOT a biennium type.
rule: When triaging UNESCO field-office support tickets reporting 'insufficient budget' or 'red notification' on SES/MIRO/F110 for donor (Type 101-112) funds, ALWAYS check whether the fund's project title contains an explicit biennium tag like '(2024-2025)' or '(2026-2027)'. If so, check whether a successor biennium fund exists by searching funds for FINCODE one digit higher (e.g. 196EAR4042 -> 196EAR4043) AND whether the successor's PROJ.POST1 explicitly names the new biennium. If both conditions hold, the predecessor fund is a biennium-end starvation candidate and the immediate workaround is FMAVCREINIT on (RLDNR=9H, predecessor fund, current RYEAR).

When an availability/budget incident is reported (TCODE in {ML81N, F110, F-53, MIRO, FB60, FBV0, FMBB, FMX1}, error class FMAVC*, BP6*, ZFI*, RW609 with a budget keyword), pull BOTH the FM-AVC pool AND the PS-AVC pool BEFORE declaring a root cause. Never conclude the firing engine on the basis of message vocabulary or domain-prefix alone.
why: INC-000005638 first pass concluded FM-side root cause and built a class detector with 79.5% hit rate -- which the user correctly flagged as 'too broad'. Pulling BPJA/COSP/FMAVCT showed the actual firing engine is FM-AVC at the AVC-DERIVED bucket level, not at any FIPEX or fund level. Without the PS data we could not even rule out PS-AVC, and without FMAVCT proper (vs the useless fmavct_summary) we could not see the TC bucket starvation. The fund-level FM pool was +$11.83M while the actual TC bucket was -$1.56M -- the difference between 'looks healthy' and 'every SES blocks'.
how_to_apply:
1. Resolve the WBS (PS_PSP_PNR) for every PO line via EKKN.
2. Compute PS-AVC pool at the project level (sum BPJA WRTTP=41 minus COSP WRTTP=04+22 across the biennium).
3. Compute FM-AVC pool at the AVC-DERIVED bucket: revenue (FMIFIIT WRTTP=66 with FIPEX in the FMAFMAP013500109 derivation range for that fund) MINUS consumption (FMAVCT KBFC for the matching bucket).
4. Tag the firing engine: BOTH if both pools < 0, FM if only FM, PS if only PS. Cite TIER_1 evidence: file:line for code, rfc_pull for data.
5. Only after the engine is identified, recommend a fix path.

rule: If revenue (WRTTP=66) is loaded on a placeholder FIPEX (commonly 'REVENUE') while consumption lands on operational FIPEX values, AND the AVC derivation rule (FMAFMAP013500109 step 0007) does NOT include the placeholder FIPEX in the same range as the operational ones, the AVC bucket sees zero revenue and full consumption — pool goes negative even though the fund-level pool is healthy. This is a SYSTEMIC pattern across UNESCO Type 101-112 funds (1,330 buckets in Tier 2 of the misalignment classifier as of 2026-05-01). It is NOT biennium-specific.
why: INC-000005638 is the first concrete instance proven with TIER_1 RFC data. Without recognising this pattern, the agent will (a) chase per-fund or per-FIPEX deficits as the root cause, (b) recommend FMAVCREINIT or biennium close-out which do NOT fix the underlying mismatch, (c) miss the systemic scale of the issue (1,787 buckets affected across UNESCO).
how_to_apply:
When examining an FM-AVC pool deficit:
1. Pull FMAFMAP013500109 entries for the fund and identify the AVC-derived range.
2. Check whether revenue (WRTTP=66) FIPEX values ARE INCLUDED in any rule range. If they are loaded on a FIPEX that is NOT in any range (e.g. 'REVENUE'), the misalignment exists.
3. Recommend either (a) extend the AVC derivation rule to include the revenue FIPEX, OR (b) refactor the revenue-posting integration (often MuleSoft for UNESCO) to apportion across operational FIPEX. Both fix the class at once.

rule: When pulling FMAVCT, ALWAYS include RFUND, RFUNDSCTR, RCMMTITEM and ALLOCTYPE_9 in the field list -- they are non-key tracking columns but they are the ONLY way to identify which (Fund x FundCenter x AVC-bucket) the row belongs to. The primary key COBJNR is an opaque 36-char internal hash. RCMMTITEM holds the AVC-DERIVED bucket (PC/TC/NPC or literal FIPEX), NOT the original FIPEX from the posting.
why: First INC-005638 extraction pulled (RLDNR, RFIKRS, COBJNR, RYEAR, ALLOCTYPE_9, RTCUR, HSL01, HSLVT) — 8 fields, the safe ceiling. Result: every row had identical opaque COBJNR and the data was useless for AVC bucket analysis. Re-pulling with (RFIKRS, RFUND, RFUNDSCTR, RCMMTITEM, RYEAR, ALLOCTYPE_9, HSL01) revealed the actual TC vs 80 vs literal-FIPEX bucket structure.
how_to_apply: Slim 7-field set: RFIKRS, RFUND, RFUNDSCTR, RCMMTITEM, RYEAR, ALLOCTYPE_9, HSL01. If you need additional periods, do a second pull with HSL02-HSL16 keyed on the same row identifiers.

rule: UNESCO's FMAVCT only stores ALLOCTYPE_9='KBFC' (consumption) rows -- never KBFB (budget). The pool depth at any AVC bucket must be computed JOINING FMIFIIT (revenue side, WRTTP=66) and FMAVCT (consumption side, KBFC). Querying FMAVCT alone for 'budget vs consumption' is WRONG.
why: Default mental model is FMAVCT has both budget and consumption rows. UNESCO's config does not. Several FM-AVC analyses across sessions inferred 'fund is depleted' from FMAVCT alone -- they were measuring consumption only, not pool depth.
how_to_apply: Pool depth = sum(FMIFIIT FKBTR WHERE FONDS=F AND FISTL=FC AND WRTTP=66 AND GJAHR=Y AND FIPEX in derivation_range_for_bucket(B)) MINUS sum(FMAVCT HSL01 WHERE RFUND=F AND RFUNDSCTR=FC AND RCMMTITEM=B AND RYEAR=Y AND ALLOCTYPE_9='KBFC').

rule: RFC_READ_TABLE on EKKN has a hard 8-field ceiling. Pulling 9+ fields raises AD/E/718 (TABLE_WITHOUT_DATA / buffer overflow) even on tiny WHERE clauses. Same applies to BPJA, BPDJ, COSP, COSS — all wide tables.
why: Discovered 2026-05-01 during INC-005638 extension. Initial extraction with 25 fields failed cryptically; the splitter fallback worked but required recursion. The cleanest path is to plan a slim 7-8 field set up front based on what the analysis actually needs.
how_to_apply:
When designing a new RFC extraction for any table with > 50 fields:
1. Write down the 5-7 columns the analysis truly needs.
2. Add 1-2 join-key columns to enable downstream JOINs.
3. Verify total row width < ~250 bytes (each char field ~16-24 bytes, each CURR/QUAN ~16 bytes).
4. If you need more, plan a second pull keyed on the same row identifiers. Do NOT rely on the recursive splitter -- it loses the row-alignment guarantee on heterogeneous WHEREs.

rule: Before describing SAP mechanism behavior in companions, specs, or operator playbooks, validate against SAP Help Portal + screenshots of the actual customer system. Brain claims, intuition, or session-derived models can be wrong on mechanisms that have not been exercised in production yet.
why: Session #66 (2026-05-01): the companion's V001 deployment strategy was built on an 'atomic flag flip via EX_STATUS' model with 'rollback in seconds'. Deep research against SAP Help Portal (Version Management, Activating Format Trees, function module DMEE_GET_BACK_ACTIVE_TREE_ABA, R3TR DMEE workbench class confirmation) + 5 tx DMEE screenshots from UNESCO P01 revealed the real SAP-standard behavior is fundamentally different: V001 activation OVERWRITES V000 (content replacement, not flag flip); rollback requires a Generate Version snapshot taken BEFORE activation (not pre-positioned transport); transport class is Workbench (R3TR DMEE), not Customizing. Brain claim 102 said 'first-ever V001 transport at UNESCO' which was true but the team had built deployment mechanics on assumptions about how that transport would behave at activation — assumptions that did not match SAP standard. The wrong model would have caused: (a) V000 unrecoverable after Phase 5 cutover (no snapshot prep step), (b) failed rollback procedure under pressure, (c) misclassified transport-class approval chain (W vs K reviewer requirements differ). Caught this session because user pushed back on the magic-feeling explanation and demanded SAP-official sources.
how_to_apply:
When writing about SAP mechanism behavior (DMEE versioning, BAdI dispatch, transport semantics, F110 internals, BCM workflow logic, etc.) in any operator-facing artifact:
1. Identify each load-bearing mechanism claim ('atomic flip', 'rollback in seconds', 'snapshot preserved', 'transport class W', etc.).
2. For each claim, find SAP-Help-Portal-level evidence OR a screenshot from the actual customer system OR SAP-shipped function module documentation. Brain TIER_1 claims about UNESCO state are NOT sufficient evidence for SAP mechanism behavior — those are about UNESCO, not about SAP standard.
3. If evidence is missing, mark the claim '[INFERRED]' or '[VERIFICATION PENDING]'. Do not present unverified mechanism claims as operational instructions.
4. For Phase 5-style cutover plans specifically: validate the cutover and rollback procedure end-to-end against SAP-official docs before publishing to operators. Mistakes on cutover mechanics are high-impact (production payment files, bank acceptance, audit trail).
5. When pushing back from a user surfaces a 'this looks like magic' / 'I do not see this in the UI' moment: take it seriously, do the deep research, do not defend the existing model.
6. After a correction is applied, delete the contradicting content (do not leave it as 'historical') — the SAP-CORRECTION callout itself is the historical record.
cp_link_reason: CP-003 (Precision, evidence, facts) — the rule is a direct application: every operational claim must be anchored in maximum precision + verifiable evidence + checkable facts. Brain claims are necessary but not sufficient when the claim is about SAP mechanism behavior; SAP-Help-Portal-level sources or live system screenshots are required. The session #66 correction (DMEE versioning model) was the second-order CP-003 violation: the brain had TIER_1 facts about UNESCO state (claim 109 V001 byte-equal V000) but the deployment strategy was layered on top with TIER_3 inferred mechanism behavior treated as TIER_1. The fix forces the verification gate at the boundary between project facts and SAP mechanism claims.

violations_observed.evidence: Companion described V001 cutover as 'atomic flag flip on EX_STATUS, rollback in seconds via flip back, V000 preserved automatically' — all three claims contradicted by SAP Help Portal which says activation overwrites V000 with V001 content; rollback requires Version Management retrieve of a pre-saved snapshot; preservation requires manual Generate Version before activation. 380 lines of lifecycle/playbook content had to be deleted and replaced after deep research.

rule: Before settling on a Phase-3-style testing methodology for a SAP runtime change, systematically walk the tx-level Test/Simulate menu options of the affected module. SAP runtime engines (DMEE, SAPFPAYM, BAdI test harnesses, etc.) typically expose their runtime input structures directly in a built-in test mode. These test modes accept manual or copy-pasted data and run the engine against it without upstream stages — enabling history-replay testing without F110 (or equivalent upstream caller).
why: Session #66 (2026-05-01): the project had a Python simulator (claim 105) for fast schema validation and a planned 'Activate V001 in D01 + F110' for full-stack validation. The middle ground — tx DMEE → Tree → Test with hand-crafted FPAYHX/FPAYH/FPAYP — was overlooked entirely until the user spotted the screen layout and pointed out that 'the columns ARE the runtime buffers, F110 just fills them automatically'. This unlocked layer 3 of the testing methodology: SAP-engine-accurate validation against historical production patterns (REGUH/REGUP reconstruction → paste → run) without requiring F110 in any system. Without this layer, Phase 3 testing was scheduled to depend on D01 F110 batch runs which are 30 min each and require the V001 activation transport. With layer 3, the top-15 scenarios (94.5% volume coverage) can be validated in ~30 min TOTAL using REGUH/REGUP reconstruction + paste-and-run in tx DMEE Test Data. As a derivative benefit, the test screen reveals which V001 MP_SC_FLD bindings are SAP-standard (visible) vs UNESCO-custom append (hidden in CI_FPAYHX) — a portability audit by inspection.
how_to_apply:
1. When designing a Phase-3 test strategy for any SAP runtime change, list the tx-codes that drive the runtime chain.
2. For each tx-code, walk the menu items: look for Test, Simulate, Trial, 'Display Test Data', or similar — they are usually under Tree/Tools/Utilities/Goto menus.
3. If a Test mode exposes input structures: those structures are the runtime entry point — testing can start there, skipping upstream stages.
4. Document the test mode in the testing-methodology section of the spec/companion alongside any pure-software simulator and any full-stack integration test.
5. Stratify test cases across the available layers (typical 4 layers): (a) fast/cheap simulator for design iteration; (b) SAP-native test mode hand-crafted for engine-accuracy spot-checks; (c) SAP-native test mode + database-reconstructed history for production-pattern coverage; (d) full-stack with real upstream invocation for final integration.
6. Critically: examine which fields are visible in the test mode by default — they are the SAP-standard runtime structure. Fields hidden in 'More Fields' or append-structure layouts are customer extensions; bindings to those are non-portable to other systems.
cp_link_reason: CP-001 (Knowledge over velocity) — this is a discovery-discipline rule. The DMEE Test Data feature was always present in tx DMEE but never inspected during Phase 0-1 testing-methodology design. Velocity prioritised 'we have a Python simulator + D01 F110, that's enough' over the slower act of walking the SAP transaction menus to find what else was already available. The cost of that velocity was an avoidable gap in the testing layers (no SAP-engine-accurate middle layer between simulator and full F110). The rule forces a discovery pass before testing-methodology lock-in.

violations_observed.evidence: Phase 0/1 testing methodology was designed with 2 layers (Python simulator + D01 F110) and the project shipped to Phase 2 build with that plan. The 3rd layer (tx DMEE → Tree → Test with FPAYHX/FPAYH/FPAYP buffer-paste) was discovered Session #66 only because the user took a screenshot of the DMEE Test Data screen and recognised the input structures as the runtime buffers F110 fills. Had this discovery happened in Phase 0, the testing matrix would have been planned differently and Phase 3 effort estimate would have been ~30 min for top-15 scenarios instead of N hours of D01 F110 batch coordination.

title: When user reports budget exceeded on UNESCO funds, ALWAYS test BOTH FM-AVC bucket and PS-AVC pool BEFORE attributing to one engine
why: INC-000005638 demonstrated that 'insuffisance de budget' from a UNESCO user is ambiguous: PS-AVC project pool can be +$16M while FM-AVC TC bucket is in -$1.5M deficit on the SAME (Fund, FundCenter) tuple. Inferring engine from user terminology is unsafe.
how_to_apply: Before attributing a 'budget exceeded' incident to PS-AVC OR FM-AVC, compute both pools: (a) PS-AVC = sum bpja_*.WTJHR WRTTP=41 over the project's WBS minus sum cosp_*.WTG001..WTG003 WRTTP IN ('04','22'); (b) FM-AVC bucket = sum fmifiit_full.FKBTR WRTTP=66 in AVC-derivation FIPEX range minus sum fmavct_*.HSL01 ALLOCTYPE_9=KBFC at the (RFIKRS, RFUND, RFUNDSCTR, RCMMTITEM) bucket. Run inc5638_per_po_engine_analysis.py-style logic and report verdict={FM | PS | BOTH | NEITHER}.
anti_pattern: Defaulting to PS-AVC because the user said 'budget exceeded on a project' without testing FM-AVC at the AVC-derived bucket level.
rule: When user reports budget exceeded on UNESCO funds, ALWAYS test BOTH FM-AVC bucket and PS-AVC pool BEFORE attributing to one engine

title: When triaging an AVC budget block, ALWAYS check the class detector first to determine if it is one-off or class-of-defect
rule: When a user reports an FMAVC005 / FI 026 / 'insuffisance de budget' on a TYPE 101-112 donor fund, the FIRST action is to run the class detector inc5638_fm_ps_avc_misalignment.py against the latest Gold DB and check whether the affected (Fund, FundCenter) bucket is part of the 2,005-bucket MODEL-GAP-2026-001 class. If yes: stop investigating as a one-off, escalate as class instance. If no: proceed with per-incident analysis but capture the result in the recurring detector for future class-membership re-evaluation.
why: Session #66/67 (INC-000005638) demonstrated that an apparent 'one-off' fund-level budget block was the canonical case of a 2,005-bucket structural class growing +4.1%/month. Without class-membership awareness, incident analysts are doomed to repeatedly re-discover the same root cause from scratch on every new ticket against a TYPE 101-112 donor fund. The detector+CSV pre-computes class membership; not consulting it is a velocity loss AND an evidence loss (one-off framing leaves the class footprint hidden from management). CP-001 (knowledge over velocity) and CP-003 (evidence-anchored).
how_to_apply:
1. On ticket arrival, parse the FONDS / FUNDSCTR / CommItem (or AVC-bucket) from the user's screenshot/SU53.
2. Open Zagentexecution/quality_checks/inc5638_fm_ps_avc_misalignment.csv (latest run) and grep the (FUND, FUNDSCTR, BUCKET) tuple.
3. If the tuple appears with Tier in {1, 2}: this is an instance of MODEL-GAP-2026-001. Annotate the incident accordingly, link to canonical doc knowledge/incidents/INC-000005638_ses_block_donor_fund_avc_fipex_deficit.md, propose the standard remediation (FMAVCREINIT / FMBB / TYPE 104->106 close). Do NOT redo full root-cause analysis from scratch.
4. If the tuple does NOT appear (or appears with Tier in {3, 4}): proceed with per-incident analysis but log the result back into the detector so the next class-detector run captures it. Open a known_unknown if the bucket pattern is novel.
5. Re-run the class detector at most weekly so CSV stays current. Log the run timestamp + Tier 1/2 counts in brain_state.data_quality and check growth rate vs 2026-05-01 baseline (+4.1%/month).
anti_pattern: Re-running per-PO engine analysis from scratch on every new FMAVC005 ticket without first checking class-detector membership. Reporting an incident as 'one-off' when the (Fund, FundCenter, Bucket) is in the 2,005-bucket class.
cp_link_reason: CP-001 (knowledge over velocity) — the rule preserves class-of-defect knowledge across incident tickets so each new instance is a 30-second class-lookup, not a 30-minute re-discovery. Also touches CP-003 (precision/evidence) because class-membership lookup is anchored in a TIER_1 CSV, not analyst judgment.

rule: tx DMEE 'Format tree → Test active version' (F8) tests ONLY the version with EX_STATUS='A'. There is NO 'Test maintenance version' option in the standard menu. To test the Maintenance version (V001) with the SAP engine, V001 MUST be activated first — which (per SAP-correct lifecycle) overwrites V000 with V001 content. Therefore V001 engine-level testing requires activation, and activation requires a Generate Version snapshot of the prior V000 BEFORE activation as the rollback enabler. V001 testing is therefore a D01-only activity (never P01) with strict snapshot+activate+test+rollback discipline.
why: Session #66 (2026-05-01): the user surfaced a screenshot of the tx DMEE Format tree menu. The only test option visible was 'Test active version (F8)'. Earlier guidance assumed V001 (Maintenance) could be tested in isolation by 'switching to Maintenance version and clicking Test' — that is not how the standard menu works. SAP's design assumption is: production-grade testing of a tree happens AFTER activation, on the active state. The maintenance version is for editing, not for production-grade test runs. This constrains the 4-layer testing methodology: Layer 2-3 (DMEE Test Data) tests V000 only without activation; testing V001 with the SAP engine requires Layer 4 (D01 activation with snapshot+rollback). The Python simulator (Layer 1) is therefore essential for V001 design iteration, with engine equivalence proven on V000 transitively.
how_to_apply:
1. When designing a DMEE test methodology, distinguish two separate engine-level test paths: (a) V000 testing — works directly in any system via F8 'Test active version' on the production state, no activation needed; (b) V001 testing — requires activation in a non-production system (D01) with the SAP-correct 4-step ritual: snapshot V000 to historical version (Generate Version → V002), activate V001 (overwrites V000), test the new V000 (= V001 content), retrieve V002 to restore original V000.
2. NEVER attempt V001 engine testing in P01. The activation overwrite is the same in any system; only D01 has the rollback latitude (V01 is shared UAT, P01 is production).
3. Maintain the Python simulator (or equivalent) as Layer 1 for V001 design iteration without engine testing. The simulator's V001 prediction is trusted by transitive equivalence once L1 V000 ≡ L2 (engine) V000 is empirically confirmed for the same scenarios.
4. In test runbooks, label phases explicitly: 'Phase A — Test V000 (any system, no activation)' vs 'Phase B — Test V001 (D01 only, activation+rollback ritual mandatory)'. Do not let operators conflate the two.
5. When documenting V001 test procedure, always include the snapshot pre-step and the rollback post-step — they are not optional.
cp_link_reason: CP-003 (Precision, evidence, facts) — the rule corrects an imprecise earlier claim. Initial guidance said 'switch to Maintenance version and run Test' as if both V000 and V001 testing were symmetric in tx DMEE. The screenshot from the user proved otherwise — SAP exposes only 'Test active version' (F8). The earlier framing was inferred from SAP help docs without checking the actual menu. The rule forces verification of the test-mode UI against the actual customer system before publishing operator-facing procedures, and explicitly distinguishes engine-level V000 testing (free) from engine-level V001 testing (requires activation+rollback discipline).

violations_observed.evidence: Excel runbook (sepa_ct_unes_test_cases.xlsx, first version) instructed operators to test V001 by 'switching to Maintenance version and clicking Test/Run' — that path does not work in the standard tx DMEE menu. User pushed back with the menu screenshot showing 'Test active version' is the only option. Runbook re-issued with explicit 17-step procedure for each case: 9 steps for V000 (Phase A) + 6 steps for V001 activate/test/rollback in D01 (Phase B) + 2 steps for diff.

rule: When analyzing UNESCO SAP architecture defects, the agent role is EVALUATIVE not PRESCRIPTIVE. Do not propose code modifications, BAdI implementations, or architectural changes as if the agent were going to execute them. Document findings as OPTIONS for UNESCO config teams to evaluate.
why: User directive Session #69 (2026-05-02): "No debes tocar ningún código, solo evaluar". The agent does not own or modify production SAP code. Code changes belong to UNESCO config teams (FM/PS Configuration Team, MuleSoft Ops, Architecture Board). The agent provides empirical evidence, risk classification, and structured options — UNESCO decides and executes.
how_to_apply: Reframe all "FIX-X" entries from "we propose to modify" to "option UNESCO can evaluate". Use language like "if UNESCO decides to modify X, the empirical effect would be Y" rather than "we propose modifying X". Companions and briefs should be evaluative reports, not implementation plans. Keep the analytical depth; remove any executive verbs that imply agent will execute changes.

rule: When designing DMEE V001 changes for production deployment, the ONLY definitive validation is an empirical XML output test from F110 + SAPFPAYM in a real environment (D01 dev minimum). RFC table extracts (REGUH/ADRC), brain claims about buffer populating mechanisms, and pattern-mirror reasoning across DMEE trees are NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. The runtime context binding (which field maps to which XML scope) cannot be predicted from static analysis alone.
why: Session 2026-05-07: V001 SEPA Dbtr design used FPAYH-ZSTRA for <StrtNm> source mirroring ICTP pattern. RFC extracts (REGUH-ZSTRA + ADRC UNESCO HQ) gave false confidence — REGUH had vendor data, ADRC had paying co data, and we assumed Z-include populated FPAYH-ZSTRA contextually based on Dbtr/Cdtr scope. WRONG. F110 runtime populates FPAYH-ZSTRA with vendor address regardless of XML scope. Empirical XML output (file UNES_SOGE_03SEP.in collector 10002B 2026-05-07) showed <StrtNm>BFM/FAS/PAY</StrtNm> (vendor street) instead of expected <StrtNm>Place de Fontenoy</StrtNm> (UNESCO HQ). Same test also revealed CM005 GENERIC does NOT fire automatically without OBPM3 registration — BldgNb + PstCd rendered empty. Without empirical XML test these 2 design flaws would have transported to V01/P01 and broken SEPA payments at bank schema validation level.
how_to_apply: Before any V001 transport release: 1) F110 + SAPFPAYM_MERGE end-to-end test in D01 (or dev system) — post a small payment, generate medium via SAPFPAYM_MERGE collector path, retrieve XML output from network share or FDTA. 2) Verify each PstlAdr leaf in XML matches expected for both Dbtr (paying co) AND Cdtr (vendor). 3) If D01 has BCM cross-payment-run setup blocking direct medium creation: SAPFPAYM_MERGE bypasses the gate, output goes to file system path per OBPM4 variant (UNESCO: \\hq-sapitf\SWIFT$\D01\INPUT\). 4) Skip-empirical paths (REGUH analysis only, brain claims only, pattern-mirror reasoning) are valid for hypothesis but NEVER for design closure. 5) The empirical test cost is ~30 min D01 work; the cost of skipping is potential broken production payments at bank rejection level.

rule: Before describing how to do a SAP customizing action (e.g. wire a customer FM to a DMEE event, register a payment format, create a country variant), search the existing knowledge corpus for the canonical SAP-std transaction or IMG path FIRST. Do not invent SM30 / SE16 / direct table maintenance suggestions. If the user pushes back with 'this doesn't exist as a table', do NOT defend the suggestion — accept the correction and find the standard tx.
why: Session #70 (2026-05-07): I told user `tx SM30 → V_T042FB → INSERT row` to register CM005 for SEPA Event 05. User correctly pushed back: 'esto no existe como tabla. No deberiamos reinventar la rueda esto es mas que comun'. The right answer was tx OBPM3 (Customer Enhancement / Function modules per format) — documented in our own repo at knowledge/domains/Payment/dme_creation_payment.md §2.3 line 72-73 since previous sessions. SAP has had OBPM3 since ECC 6.0; treating Payment Medium Workbench customizing as something requiring SM30 reinvention is a beginner-level error and propagates through to companion artifacts and execution runbooks.
how_to_apply:
1. For ANY SAP customizing action (DMEE FM register, format/variant create, BAdI wiring, payment method setup), ALWAYS first grep `knowledge/domains/Payment/` and similar domain folders for the canonical TX name. dme_creation_payment.md has the full OBPM1/OBPM2/OBPM3/OBPM4 quartet with screenshots and IMG paths.

rule: Before designing or transporting any V001 (or V00x) extension to a DMEE payment medium format tree, verify the format's SAP lifecycle status: open tx OBPM1 / SE16 TFPM (table for PMW formats) / search SAP Notes for 'obsolete <format_name>'. rule: Before writing WHEN clauses in YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK_CM001 GET_CREDIT (or any country variant) to handle a new DMEE tag, FIRST check whether the UNESCO PPC framework (YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_UTIL.GET_TAG_VALUE_FROM_CUSTO + YTFI_PPC_TAG + YTFI_PPC_STRUC) already covers the requirement via Z-table config. The PPC framework was built by N_MENARD 2024-09-06 specifically as the config-driven dispatcher for tag-value resolution: domains YD_FI_PPC_CODE (5 values: SEPARATOR/FIXED_VAL/PPC_VAR/PPC_DESCR/PAY_FIELD) + YD_FI_PAY_STRUC (FPAYH/FPAYHX/FPAYP). New DMEE tags activated for any country should be added as Z-table rows (YTFI_PPC_TAG entry mapping LAND1+DEB_CRE+TAG_FULL to TAG_ID; YTFI_PPC_STRUC entries with PPC_CODE rules) — not as ABAP WHEN clauses. Only when the existing PPC_CODE values cannot resolve the value (e.g. need ADRC read for paying-co address, no FPAYH-Z field populated) should ABAP delta be considered, and the delta should EXTEND the PPC framework (new PPC_CODE in domain YD_FI_PPC_CODE + UTIL.CM003 case) — never bypass it with bespoke WHEN clauses in FALLBACK_CM001.
why: Session #71 (2026-05-08): For V001 SEPA Dbtr structured-address I proposed extending YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK_CM001 GET_CREDIT with 3-4 WHEN clauses reading ADRC via T001-ADRNR (~30 LOC). rule: INSERT REPORT on a function-group include (e.g. LYFPAYMU19) DESTROYS the FUPARAREF interface metadata for the function modules in that include. After every INSERT REPORT on such an include, ALWAYS execute `GENERATE REPORT '<FUNCTION_GROUP>'` (e.g. SAPLYFPAYM) in the same one-shot to repopulate FUPARAREF.
why: Session #073 (2026-05-09): deployed Y_FI_DMEE_ADR v2 via INSERT REPORT on LYFPAYMU19. The FM source updated correctly (REPOSRC R3STATE='A'), but FUPARAREF returned TABLE_WITHOUT_DATA — interface metadata was wiped. Symptoms: RPY_FUNCTIONMODULE_READ_NEW returns 0 lines; DMEE editor reports DMEE_ABA358 'incorrect interface'; FM may execute partially (cached compiled code) or fail silently per call. The fix was an explicit `GENERATE REPORT 'SAPLYFPAYM'` which restored 11 FUPARAREF rows from the `*"` interface comments in the source.
how_to_apply:
Whenever updating a function-module body via INSERT REPORT on its include:
1. INSERT REPORT 'L<FG>U<NN>' FROM lt_src DIRECTORY ENTRY ls_trdir.
2. COMMIT WORK.
3. GENERATE REPORT 'SAPL<FG>' MESSAGE lv_msg.
4. Verify: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='Y_xxx' — should be > 0.
5. If still empty, the GENERATE failed silently — investigate before assuming the FM is OK.
The RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN one-shot must include both INSERT and GENERATE in one program so they execute under the same transaction.

rule: `GENERATE REPORT '<FG>'` regenerates the function-group code BUT does NOT re-parse the `*"` interface comments to update existing FUPARAREF rows. To change a parameter's pass-by-reference flag (VALUE→REFERENCE or vice versa), you must `UPDATE fupararef SET reference='X' WHERE funcname=... AND parameter=...` directly via ABAP one-shot, then GENERATE again.
why: Session #073 (2026-05-09): edited Y_FI_DMEE_ADR `*"` comments to change `VALUE(I_EXTENSION)` → `REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION)` (matching DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA). Deployed via INSERT REPORT + GENERATE REPORT. FUPARAREF still showed `reference=' '` (blank=VALUE) for I_EXTENSION. DMEE_ABA358 errors persisted. Fix: explicit UPDATE fupararef SET reference='X' WHERE funcname='Y_FI_DMEE_ADR' AND parameter='I_EXTENSION'. Then re-GENERATE. The errors disappeared.
how_to_apply:
When changing FM interface in `*"` comments (pass-by-value vs reference, optional flag, type, structure):
1. Edit the source `*"` comments and INSERT REPORT.
2. GENERATE REPORT '<FG>' (regenerates code but NOT FUPARAREF flags).
3. SELECT * FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='Y_xxx' — verify each parameter's `reference`, `optional`, `structure` matches the new comments.
4. For any mismatch, UPDATE fupararef SET <flag>='<new>' WHERE funcname=... AND parameter=...
5. COMMIT WORK + GENERATE REPORT '<FG>' again.
6. Re-verify FUPARAREF and run the FM via SE37 or actual caller to confirm.
Key FUPARAREF columns: PARAMETER, PARAMTYPE (I/E/C/T), STRUCTURE, OPTIONAL, REFERENCE, PPOSITION, R3STATE.

rule: DMEE exit function modules (those configured as MP_EXIT_FUNC in DMEE_TREE_NODE) MUST have an interface that EXACTLY matches one of the two SAP templates: DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_ABA (legacy) or DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA (modern, with REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION)). Any deviation triggers DMEE_ABA358 'function module XXX has incorrect interface' and the tree validation refuses to compile.
why: Session #073 (2026-05-09): Y_FI_DMEE_ADR had `VALUE(I_EXTENSION)` while DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA has `REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION)`. The mismatch produced 8 DMEE_ABA358 errors (one per Dbtr/PstlAdr/* leaf assigned to Y_FI_DMEE_ADR). Runtime sometimes tolerates the mismatch (executes with a cached compile), but tree-editor validation, transport activation, and Test mode all reject. Strict-match is enforced field-by-field in FUPARAREF: parameter name, paramtype (I/E/C/T), structure, reference flag, optional flag, position.
how_to_apply:
Before assigning a custom FM as a DMEE node exit:
1. SELECT * FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA' (the reference).
2. SELECT * FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='<your custom FM>'.
3. Diff the two: every field — PARAMETER, PARAMTYPE, STRUCTURE, OPTIONAL, REFERENCE, PPOSITION — must match.
4. If mismatch, fix via INSERT REPORT (source comments) + UPDATE fupararef (reference flag) + GENERATE REPORT.
5. Test by running tx DMEE → tree → Validate / Test active version. Should be zero DMEE_ABA358.
Reference template (extended): `IMPORTING VALUE(I_TREE_TYPE) TYPE DMEE_TREETYPE_ABA, VALUE(I_TREE_ID) TYPE DMEE_TREEID_ABA, VALUE(I_ITEM), VALUE(I_PARAM), VALUE(I_UPARAM), REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION) TYPE DMEE_EXIT_INTERFACE_ABA. EXPORTING REFERENCE(O_VALUE), REFERENCE(C_VALUE), REFERENCE(N_VALUE), REFERENCE(P_VALUE). TABLES I_TAB.`

rule: Every piece of code we extract from SAP (ABAP source via RPY_PROGRAM_READ, function modules, classes, includes, enhancements, BAdI implementations, BTEs) is BRAIN DATA — not transient artifacts. It must be persisted under extracted_code/<DOMAIN>/<SUBDOMAIN>/, registered in brain_v2 (annotations, claims, knowledge_docs), and linked in brain_state.json so future agents can: (1) understand how SAP works at UNESCO, (2) detect patterns across modules, (3) discover connections between elements and domains, (4) avoid re-extracting the same code, (5) audit historical SAP behavior.
