how_to_apply:
On every code extraction:
1. Save source under extracted_code/<DOMAIN>/<SUBDOMAIN>/<NAME>.abap (e.g. extracted_code/FI/DMEE_p01_canonical/YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK====CM001.abap).
2. For each new object: add an annotation to brain_v2/annotations/annotations.json with finding (1-2 sentences of what the code does), tag, flavor, related_objects, evidence_tier=TIER_1 source code, line numbers if specific.
3. For patterns spanning multiple objects: write a knowledge doc under knowledge/domains/<DOMAIN>/ and link it from the relevant brain_state.objects[X].knowledge_docs.
4. For author/team-ownership: capture in annotation 'author' field (e.g. 'N_MENARD') so future agents respect feedback_only_modify_our_own_code.
5. Run brain_v2/rebuild_all.py at session close to refresh brain_state.json.
6. Cross-reference: when extracting object X, check brain_state.objects[X] first — if already annotated, only add new findings, do not duplicate.
7. NEVER let extracted_code/ rot — it is a first-class persistence layer of the project.

rule: Rule: when emitting a vendor address from any UNESCO output (DMEE, avisos, F110 confirms, BCM print, treasury report), check PA0006 SUBTY='1' BEFORE reading ADRC.STREET. Cast LIFNR → PERNR via NUMC(8). If PA0006 hits → employee path (real home address). If not → vendor path (ADRC). The dispatch is KTOKK-agnostic — explicit KTOKK='SCSA' branching (the v5 design) misses cases where staff are paid against KTOKK=UNES / INDV / ICVS LIFNRs.
why: Session #073 (2026-05-08): Y_FI_DMEE_ADR v5 used explicit KTOKK='SCSA' detection. F110 SEPA run for Simona BERTOLDINI emitted 'BFM/FAS/PAY' as <StrtNm> because her payment LIFNR is KTOKK=UNES (not SCSA), so v5 fell through to ADRC and printed the dept code. v6 PA0006-first detection is robust regardless of which KTOKK F110 paid against. Validated live on D01 V01T3 run — BERTOLDINI's real home address (16 avenue des Murs du Parc, 94300 Vincennes) emitted correctly. UNESCO LIFNR↔PERNR convention: PERNR = LIFNR cast NUMC(8) (e.g. 0010008305 → 10008305). ADRC.STREET stores dept codes for SCSA staff records — assuming ADRC = real address is wrong system-wide, not just SEPA-specific.
how_to_apply: (1) For any new code that emits a vendor address: SELECT SINGLE FROM PA0006 WHERE PERNR = LIFNR (NUMC8 cast) AND SUBTY='1' AND date-valid first. (2) If SY-SUBRC=0 → use PA0006-STRAS/PSTLZ/ORT01/LAND1/STATE. (3) Else fall back to ADRC of the LIFNR. (4) For audit of EXISTING code: grep for SELECT * FROM ADRC patterns where the addrnumber comes from LIFNR-related sources (LFA1-ADRNR, FPAYH-ZADNR, etc.) — every such site is a candidate for the same bug. (5) Document the convention in the affected output's spec / companion. (6) Reference: Y_FI_DMEE_ADR v6 in extracted_code/FI/DMEE_full_inventory/Y_FI_DMEE_ADR_v6.abap; knowledge/domains/Payment/vendor_address_routing_by_ktokk.md.

rule: Before claiming a custom FM (e.g. Y_FI_DMEE_ADR) fixes a payment-format bug, query DMEE_TREE_NODE.MP_EXIT_FUNC for every relevant tree to confirm the FM is actually wired. A fix only applies where the tree calls it.
why: Session #074: I initially extended the v6 simulator across all SEPA formats — but Y_FI_DMEE_ADR is wired ONLY in /SEPA_CT_UNES. The drift forecast for /SEPA_CT_ICTP_* was theoretical (would-happen-if), not in-scope. User caught this: 'no cambien nunca estos formatos cómo puede ser que funcione'. The same logic applies to /CGI_XML_CT_UNESCO and /CITI/XML/UNESCO/DC_V3_01 — they wire FI_CGI_DMEE_EXIT_W_BADI and /CITIPMW/* FMs, not Y_FI_DMEE_ADR. The fix surface is bounded by tree wiring, not by FM availability.
how_to_apply: (1) For any payment-format bug claim, query DMEE_TREE_NODE for the affected leaves with MP_EXIT_FUNC populated. (2) Separate 'in-scope' (FM is wired) from 'theoretical' (FM would fix if wired). (3) When reporting drift across formats, label each row as IN-SCOPE or OUT-OF-SCOPE based on tree wiring evidence, not on assumed coverage. (4) Reference: extracted DMEE_TREE_NODE topology for the 5 active formats in claim 185.

rule: DFPAYG (execution evidence) and DFPAYV (config matrix) are the canonical source for any 'which payment format/run/vendor' question. Always cross-reference both before answering scope or coverage questions about UNESCO payments.
why: Session #074 added both tables to Gold DB. DFPAYG = 9,848 rows = ground truth for what actually fired in the last 2 years; DFPAYV = 84 rows = static config showing what CAN fire (with 6 lapsed configs that never run). Combined with REGUH, they let SQL answer: 'which staff vendor was paid via which format×cocode×bank×account×PM combination?' — replacing ad-hoc P01 RFC queries.
how_to_apply: (1) Format scope questions: SELECT DISTINCT FORMI FROM DFPAYG WHERE LAUFD >= '<window>' (= active set); SELECT FORMI FROM DFPAYV (= configured set); difference = lapsed configs. (2) Vendor questions: JOIN DFPAYG to REGUH on (LAUFD, LAUFI, ZBUKR) to get the vendor list paid via each format. (3) Bank/account/PM granularity: REGUH_FAST has HBKID, HKTID, RZAWE — better than DFPAYG for the routing breakdown. (4) Indexes: idx_reguh_run on (LAUFD,LAUFI,ZBUKR), idx_dfpayg_formi, idx_dfpayg_zbukr.

rule: When reporting payment metrics, ALWAYS label whether the count is 'distinct LIFNRs' or 'REGUH payment lines'. Same employee paid 30 times = 1 distinct LIFNR = 30 lines. The two scales differ by 5-30x in typical UNESCO data.
why: Session #074 user clarification: 'O sea son la cantidades de pagos staff que se hacen para ese formato' — user assumed 'staff drift = number of payments' but my number was 'distinct staff vendors'. The actual XMLs emitted = REGUH lines, not vendors. For /SEPA_CT_UNES UNES 2025-26: 1,659 staff vendors but 12,107 lines (7.3x factor).
how_to_apply: (1) Default to BOTH counts when reporting: e.g. '1,659 staff vendors → 12,107 lines'. (2) For business impact (XMLs emitted with wrong data, bank rejection volume), use LINES. (3) For root-cause analysis (which employees are affected), use VENDORS. (4) Include the multiplier explicitly: 'pays/vendor ratio = 7.3x'.

rule: When presenting tables to operational users, use the FULL business name for each column (Company Code, House Bank, Bank Account, Payment Method) — NOT the SAP technical abbreviation (ZBUKR, HBKID, HKTID, RZAWE) or my shorthand (COCO, BANK, ACCT, PM).
why: Session #074 user feedback: 'O faltan las columnas, Company code, house bank bank Account, and mediunm payment please' — when I used abbreviated headers, the user explicitly asked for the full names. Treasury and finance operators read SAP tables every day but the technical names slow them down vs business labels.
how_to_apply: (1) First column header row uses business names: 'Company Code (ZBUKR)' is acceptable, 'ZBUKR' alone is not. (2) Apply consistently across companions and brain output. (3) Exception: when the audience is purely technical (ABAP devs / brain agents), abbreviations are fine.

rule: RFC_READ_TABLE has narrow accepted OPTIONS syntax: (a) NO 'IN (...)' clauses — use multiple single-field calls instead; (b) leading space required when concatenating conditions (' AND TECH_NAME = ...'); (c) DATA_BUFFER_EXCEEDED on wide tables — limit FIELDS to <20 columns or expect 512-byte WA truncation. Document tables that are DMEE_TREE_NODE, REGUH, etc. often hit these limits.
why: Session #074 wasted ~15 minutes debugging OPTION_NOT_VALID errors when querying DMEE_TREE_NODE with IN clauses. Once switched to per-TECH_NAME calls in a loop, queries worked. This is a recurring pattern across sessions but never captured as a rule.
how_to_apply: (1) When OPTION_NOT_VALID appears, simplify OPTIONS: one condition per row, leading space on continuation rows, no IN clauses. (2) For multi-value filtering, loop the query per value instead. (3) When DATA_BUFFER_EXCEEDED hits, narrow FIELDS list or split into multiple narrow queries. (4) Verified working pattern: OPTIONS=[{'TEXT':"TREE_ID = '/X'"}, {'TEXT':" AND TECH_NAME = 'StrtNm'"}]. Bad: OPTIONS=[{'TEXT':"TREE_ID='/X' AND TECH_NAME IN ('StrtNm','BldgNb')"}].

rule: When SAP auth fails, ALWAYS test the same credentials via both RFC (port 3300) AND HTTP (port 80) before declaring 'password is wrong'. SAP commonly accepts the same user/password on one protocol while rejecting it on another — caused by SU01 user type, USR02 password-buffer desync, or SICF policy. Run the 60-second diagnostic in unescrp/.claude/skills/sap-fiori-react-builder/sap-fiori-react-builder/references/deployment/sap-d01-connection-patterns.md before opening a credentials INC.
why: Session #075: unescrp project burned 2+ hours assuming the 40-char password was stale, including retrying passwords found in earlier .env snapshots and probing /sap/bc/adt/discovery 6 times. The same password authenticates cleanly via RFC. Root cause is SAP-side ICF/SU01 — none of the client-side fixes would have helped. Isolating protocol vs credentials would have saved the time and triggered the correct BASIS ticket immediately.
how_to_apply: (1) First failure to authenticate → run RFC probe (pyrfc T000 read). (2) If RFC works → it's not the password; switch to HTTP probe (urllib Basic + ADT discovery). (3) If RFC fails → check .env / VPN / SNC config. (4) If RFC works AND HTTP fails → SAP-side, open BASIS ticket with the diagnostic evidence. Don't keep trying passwords. (5) Document the result in the project's connection-patterns reference file.

rule: Do NOT trust `sap_adt_client.fetch_csrf()` or any `_request()` call as proof of HTTP auth success. The current `_request` implementation catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` and returns `(status, body, headers)` without raising — and SAP echoes a CSRF token even on 401 when `X-CSRF-Token: Fetch` is sent. Always assert `status == 200` after the call. Patch `_request()` to raise on 4xx, or replace the client with one that propagates errors.
why: Session #075: I told the user 'ADT HTTP works' based on `fetch_csrf()` returning normally, then realized the client silently swallowed the 401 and returned an empty token. The mistake cost trust and required a public correction. The bug has likely caused false positives in other sessions where ADT 'success' messages preceded mysterious downstream failures.
how_to_apply: (1) When calling sap_adt_client methods, check the returned status code explicitly, not just whether a value came back. (2) Add a fix to `_request`: `if status >= 400: raise HTTPError(...)`. (3) Same patch needed for fetch_csrf, search_object, get_source, etc. (4) Until patched, run a separate `urllib.request.urlopen` probe to confirm 200 before trusting the client.

rule: When another project (Tier 2 application or sibling Tier 1) consumes this brain, SAP-system facts (tables, transactions, standard customizing, customer customizing in any SAP module) MUST live ONLY in abapobjectscreation/brain_v2. The consuming project cites by reference (path + node id) and never duplicates. Project-specific facts (Z objects the consumer is building, design decisions, application-internal taxonomy) live in the consumer's brain.
why: Session #00 of FINCLOSSING (2026-05-23) — first Tier 2 application project that needs to consume SAP truth without forking it. Without this rule, two brains will diverge on facts like 'BKPF columns' or 'CLOCO table layout' and the failure mode (silent drift) is invisible until an agent makes a wrong decision against a stale copy. Plausibility-without-evidence (CP-003 violation) is the concrete failure pattern.
how_to_apply: (1) Before writing a fact to a consumer's brain, ask: 'is this about SAP itself, or about what the consumer is BUILDING?' (2) If about SAP → grep abapobjectscreation/brain_v2 first; if missing, ADD it to abapobjectscreation, not the consumer. (3) If about the consumer's Z objects / design / app-internal taxonomy → consumer's brain is correct. (4) Each consumer maintains a `refs_external.json` listing every layer/file it reads from this brain — that is the canonical drift-detection surface. (5) Reverse pointer: this brain maintains `brain_v2/consumers.md` listing every project that depends on it, so refactors here check downstream impact.

rule: When prior analysis has converged on an obvious recommended path AND the user signals agreement (OK/si/dale/proceed), do NOT present a 3-option AskUserQuestion menu. Execute the recommendation directly. The agent OWNS the technical decision.
why: During session #076 ADT expansion, after a long analysis that converged on Build now + BASIS ticket in parallel, I still presented a 3-option menu. User rejected the tool use and said OK proceed im not sure what you need from basis. Menus are friction when path is obvious. Reinforces existing rule feedback_own_the_decision_stop_asking.
how_to_apply:
1. If my prior message ended with clear recommendation + user agrees (OK/si/dale/proceed), do not present options. Execute.
2. Reserve AskUserQuestion for genuinely-equivalent-tradeoff cases or when user has not yet given any signal.
3. When the user signals lack of context (not sure what X means), do NOT ask them to choose - give them what they need or just decide for them and explain.
4. If I find myself drafting an AskUserQuestion after a long analysis, delete it and proceed.

rule: Before recommending any SAP capability (ADT endpoint, BAPI, RFC FM, transaction availability), VERIFY it exists on the target kernel via empirical probe. SAP NetWeaver capabilities differ across releases - what works in S/4HANA / NW 7.5x may be 404 on UNESCO ECC 6.0 EhP8 (NW 7.40). Never assume kernel-uniform.
why: Session #076 violation: I confidently recommended ADT REST define_table / create_index as the canonical DDIC path, including copy-paste prompts for the parallel unescrp conversation. Then user tested empirically and confirmed /sap/bc/adt/ddic/tables returns HTTP 404 on D01 (NW 7.40) - endpoint shipped in NW 7.50. ~400 lines of code became S/4HANA scaffolding, cross-project recommendation had to be retracted before being applied.
how_to_apply:
1. Before recommending an ADT method, call adt_discovery() and grep the response for the relevant collection. If endpoint absent, the method will 404 - recommend RFC alternative instead.
2. Before recommending a BAPI / RFC FM, run RFC_READ_TABLE FROM TFDIR WHERE FUNCNAME EQ name to confirm availability.
3. Before recommending a transaction, verify via TSTCT or quick GUI probe.
4. UNESCO landscape baseline: ECC 6.0 EhP8 = NW 7.40. Treat any capability described as NW 7.5+ or S/4HANA-only as unavailable until proven otherwise.
5. When recommending a path that crosses kernel versions, be explicit about version requirement IN THE RECOMMENDATION.
6. When a recommendation is later proven wrong by empirical evidence, revise the related memory rules IMMEDIATELY and acknowledge the error directly - no softening.

rule: For ANY new ABAP/DDIC object work (create table, DE, domain, class, program, FM, index, etc.), the agent works EXCLUSIVELY in D01. NEVER touches P01 - not for write, not for read, not for preflight, not for does this exist. The only legitimate P01 read in a creation context is post-transport verification.
why: Session #076 violation: I called from_env(P01) and ran RFC_READ_TABLE FROM DD02L WHERE TABNAME='ZCRP_CERTHEAD' to triple-confirm the table doesn't exist there. The check was logically unnecessary - by the transport model, if it doesn't exist in D01 it cannot exist in P01 - and crossed a boundary the user explicitly maintains. User response in CAPS: PARA NUEVOS OBJETOS LO HACEMOS EN D01!!! NUNCA P01. This rule is STRICTER than the broader no-prod-writes rule.
how_to_apply:
1. When the user mentions creating/modifying/deploying a new ABAP/DDIC object: pin the system as D01 only. Do not call from_env(P01).
2. For preflight of objects related to a new creation, query D01 only.
3. The only legitimate P01 read in a new-object context is post-transport verification - prefer STMS over RFC.
4. If user explicitly requests a P01 probe for some OTHER reason (incident, data extraction, customizing read), that is allowed under standard no-prod-writes rule.
5. If unsure whether request is new-object work or diagnosis work, ASK before touching P01.

rule: ADT-first is qualified by kernel + object class. SOURCE CODE objects (PROG/CLAS/INTF/FUGR/FUNC/INCLUDE/ENHO/XSLT/BSP) - ADT-first on ALL kernels including EhP8. DDIC objects (TABL/DTEL/DOMA/INDX) - ADT-first ONLY on NW 7.50+ / S/4HANA. On EhP8 (UNESCO D01/P01) DDIC creation MUST use the DDIF wrapper (sap_adt_client.define_table_via_ddif / define_data_element_via_ddif / define_domain_via_ddif) with TR_TADIR_INTERFACE injection and verify_tadir post-check.
why: Session #076: I originally saved a rule ADT-first for ALL DDIC, generating ABAP programs that call DDIF_*_PUT is forbidden as architecture. Empirical probe revealed ADT REST /sap/bc/adt/ddic/tables returns HTTP 404 on NW 7.40 - endpoint shipped in NW 7.50. So on EhP8 the DDIF_*_PUT via RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN pattern is NOT debt - it is the only path. Pain points (opaque RC=2, IN-list parser bug, TADIR-orphan) are real and mitigated by the wrapper, not avoided. The original rule overgeneralized and had to be corrected.
how_to_apply:
1. Before any DDIC create/modify, call adt_discovery() once and grep for the endpoint. If absent, fall back to the DDIF wrapper (NEVER to ad-hoc programs without preflight + TADIR fix).
2. For SOURCE CODE work, default to ADT REST.
3. When reviewing legacy projects for RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN + DDIF_*_PUT patterns on EhP8, do NOT mark them as debt - verify they implement preflight + TR_TADIR_INTERFACE + structured-error mitigation. If they do, the pattern is correct; if not, refactor to the wrapper, do not switch to ADT (which would fail).
4. Track the S/4HANA migration: when UNESCO upgrades, flip DDIC operations to the ADT methods (already scaffolded) - field-list and return-dict shape are identical.
5. DDIC creation order (both paths): Domain - Data Element - Table - Index. Validate prerequisites before each create.

rule: CRITICAL HARD RULE: NEVER modify, alter, extend the structure of, append fields to, change DEs of, or alter activation state of SAP-delivered standard objects. Applies to ALL tools (DDIF wrapper, ADT REST, abapGit pull, RFC FM calls, Playwright). Only Z*/Y*/customer-namespace objects can be modified. For SAP-standard extension needs, use append structures, customer includes, BAdIs, enhancement implementations, or user exits — never modify the original. Refuse the request and explain when asked to modify a standard object.
why: SAP licensing forbids unauthorized modification of delivered objects (SSCR keys required); upgrades (SPS/EhP/S/4HANA conversion) overwrite standard objects and force SPDD/SPAU manual adjustments which are manual, error-prone, and break frequently. UNESCO ECC 6.0 EhP8 is a mature production estate where standard modifications carry ongoing maintenance cost on every Support Package application — UNESCO BASIS team will refuse them on principle. Modifying a standard DE/domain cascades activation to thousands of dependent tables. A wrong TR_TADIR_INTERFACE call against a standard object can set EDTFLAG=X and break SE11 editability system-wide.
how_to_apply:
Before any DDIC/code write: check if object name is non-standard.

  def is_standard(name): return not name.upper().startswith(('Z','Y','/'))

If standard, REFUSE the call and respond:
  1. Cite this rule (feedback_never_modify_standard_objects)
  2. Explain why (SAP licensing + upgrade safety + UNESCO policy)
  3. Offer permitted alternative (append structure / customer include / BAdI / enhancement)
  4. Ask user to rephrase as Z-namespace addition

Permitted alternatives:
  - Add fields to standard table: Z append structure (CI_* include or .APPEND)
  - Modify standard FM behavior: BAdI / enhancement spot / user exit (Z implementation)
  - Modify standard class behavior: ENHO enhancement implementation
  - Customizing of standard T-tables: SM30 row CRUD = DATA changes (permitted), structure changes (forbidden)

Edge cases:
  - Customizing rows in T-tables: data changes are OK, structure changes are NOT
  - PFCG role modifications: copy to Z-named role first
  - SICF service activation: flag toggle OK; handler class modification NOT

rule: ARCHITECTURAL STANDARD: abapGit is the DEFAULT deployment path for any object type it supports (170+ types covering DDIC, source code, enhancements, OData, BSP). DDIF wrapper / ADT REST / RFC alternatives are BRIDGES or FALLBACKS for cases abapGit cannot cover OR for the period until abapGit is installed on the target system. Priority order: 1) abapGit (default for supported types when installed), 2) ADT REST (source code on all kernels, bridge for source until abapGit), 3) DDIF wrapper (DDIC on EhP8, bridge until abapGit), 4) RFC/Playwright (for objects no other tool covers: SM59, SM30 rows, SICF, RZ10, BOR, PFCG user assignments).
why: abapGit is the de-facto industry standard for SAP Z code deployment: 10+ years, 50K+ installs, SAP-promoted via TechEd. It handles TADIR/CTS architecturally correctly (uses RS_CORR_INSERT, no EDTFLAG bug), provides native version control with Git history/blame/diff/rollback, supports atomic multi-object deploys (N objects in 1 ZIP = 1 TR), is forward-compatible across kernels (EhP8/NW 7.5x/S/4HANA), enables cross-system sync (D01->QAS without STMS forward path), and supports PR-based code review. The DDIF wrapper we built is a hand-rolled subset that learned the same lessons through bugs (TADIR-orphan, EDTFLAG poisoning) that abapGit solves by design. Installation operational state (installed or not) is separate from architectural correctness (abapGit IS the standard regardless).
how_to_apply:
When proposing a deployment: lead with "if abapGit is installed, use it; otherwise the bridge is X". Don't propose the bridge as the default.

When abapGit is not installed (current D01 state): include the BASIS ticket escalation in the response, marked STRATEGIC PRIORITY (not optional). Bridge solution is temporary.

When designing new automation: API shape compatible with both backends (e.g. define_table(...) works whether backend is abapGit-pull or DDIF wrapper). Forward-compatible.

When migrating to S/4HANA: abapGit path stays. DDIF wrapper deprecates. ADT REST takes over what DDIF did, but abapGit lifecycle features remain its own value.

When auditing legacy projects (unescrp, ecosystem): check if they use abapGit. If yes, validate they're using it correctly. If no, propose migration when timing allows.

Before recommending abapGit as the immediate path: verify install via 5-way TADIR/TRDIR/TDEVC/TFDIR probe (per feedback_verify_capabilities_before_recommending). If not installed, recommend bridge with STRATEGIC install ticket attached.

rule: When assessing whether a SAP data-access restriction (note, patch, audit, security advisory) affects us, FIRST read our code to classify the EXACT function-module / API family our pipeline calls, then compare it against the SPECIFIC API the restriction names. Never reason from the category ('it is an RFC that reads data'). ODP Data Replication APIs (RODPS_REPL_*, ODQ_*, /SAPDS/) are a different framework from the generic RFC_READ_TABLE reader. UNESCO's Gold DB uses RFC_READ_TABLE only and is OUT OF SCOPE of SAP Note 3255746; the 2026-06-09 ODP-blocking patch does not affect it.
why: SAP Note 3255746 ('Unpermitted usage of ODP Data Replication APIs') triggered an 'are we affected?' question. The failure mode is reasoning from the category: assuming any data-extraction RFC is in scope. ODP is a replication framework (delta queues, subscriptions, change-data-capture); RFC_READ_TABLE is a generic single-table SELECT-equivalent with no delta queue and no subscription. Conflating them produces either a false 'we are non-compliant' panic or -- worse -- a false 'we are safe' on a note that DID hit us. Precision on the exact API IS the whole answer (CP-003: precision + evidence + facts).
how_to_apply:
1) Grep the repo for the SPECIFIC restricted FMs/namespaces named in the note (e.g. RODPS_REPL, ODQ_, /SAPDS/) -- report the call count with file:line.
2) Identify the FM our pipeline actually calls (read rfc_helpers.py / extract_*.py) and cite it.
3) Produce a restricted-vs-used comparison so the verdict is auditable.
4) Recommend running SAP's own self-assessment tool (when the note ships one, e.g. Note 3439624) to convert code evidence into SAP-sourced confirmation.
5) If the pipeline depends on a single non-released FM (RFC_READ_TABLE), flag it as a forward-looking risk and name the SAP-endorsed durable path (ODP-OData / Business Data Cloud).

rule: No research/analysis produces conclusions or plans until it is CLOSED. A research is CLOSED only when ALL 8 guarantees pass: (1) completeness, (2) graded sources, (3) adversarial verification finished, (4) citable evidence per claim, (5) explicit confidence tier, (6) gaps stated as open questions, (7) reproducibility, (8) no-spin attestation. An incomplete/stopped/failed run is OPEN -> discard or re-run; NEVER salvage its fragments into findings. Conclusions and plans are built ONLY on CLOSED claims, each carrying its tier + citation; anything on a LOW/open item is labeled ASSUMPTION/RISK.
why: s079: I presented unverified scraps from a deep research that died in Fetch (no Verify/Synthesize) as Phase-1 findings. User: 'mentiroso o irresponsable... si fuera algo medico que te parece usar un research de este nivel'. Quality discipline must be a STANDING gate, not a doc I write reactively. This is table-stakes, not a discovery.
how_to_apply: Before using ANY research output: confirm it reached Synthesize (web research = Verify(3-vote)+Synthesize ran; own analysis = each claim has path:line/query-result + tier). If not closed: say so directly, re-run, invent nothing. Label every presented item VERIFIED / INFERRED / NOT-ESTABLISHED. Do not launch web-dependent research while internet is flagged down. Phase A (close research) strictly precedes Phase B (conclusions/plans). Full spec: knowledge/research_closing_methodology.md.

rule: Every domain is modeled as a PAIR — AS-DESIGNED (standard SAP) + AS-RUN (our process) — and scored across 9 capability dimensions (S_STANDARD_REF, A_PROCESS, B_CODE, C_CONFIG, D_DATA, E_AUTH, F_INTERFACE_FILE, G_CONFORMANCE=the delta, H_IMPROVE). This domain×capability matrix (Layer 15, brain_v2/capability_model/) IS the operating model. Work is SELECTED by querying `graph_queries.py capability_gaps` — the roadmap is generated, not written. Empty COLUMNS are systemic model gaps, not per-domain. The model is PORTABLE across projects (unesco-sap-brain etc.): standard AS-DESIGNED baselines are system-invariant and shared cross-project; AS-RUN deltas are project-specific and fed back to a shared library.
why: s079: the process+code+conformance work is crucial to the MODEL, not a one-off plan. User: 'cómo lo reflejamos más allá del plan... los dominios deben ALINEARSE y luego AMPLIARSE'. A plan is consumed and archived; a model axis is queried and grows. Reflecting it structurally (4th axis) makes acquired knowledge align to one skeleton and makes every gap a deterministic, ranked work item.
how_to_apply: At session start, read brain_state.capability_model. Before proposing work, run `graph_queries.py capability_gaps` and pick from the ranked expansion_order. When a domain is touched (incident/claim/companion), update its capability cell. A capability is fully met only when BOTH strata exist AND the G delta is computed. Never present an AS-RUN finding as conformance without the AS-DESIGNED baseline (S_STANDARD_REF precondition). Keep the matrix honest: ●HAVE/◐PARTIAL/○NONE per cell with evidence. Full spec: knowledge/capability_model.md.

rule: Every CLOSED deep-research is archived under brain_v2/research/ (full result + sources + findings). Before launching ANY new deep-research, DEDUPE against brain_v2/research/sources_index.json (91 urls already read) and findings_registry.json (37 verified + 26 refuted). Do NOT re-fetch a source already analyzed or re-litigate a verified/refuted claim — READ the archive. Scope new runs to ENRICH the named openQuestions, not to repeat. Append, never overwrite. A FAILED/degraded run is logged in _run_log.json and superseded by a solo rerun — never re-run the same degraded query.
why: s079: deep-research outputs lived in EPHEMERAL temp files — they would be lost, forcing re-reads/re-runs of already-analyzed sources (waste + CP-002 violation). User: 'guarda los deep researchs para enriquecerlos en el futuro y no tener que releer algo que ya analizaste'.

rule: Distinguish TECHNICAL decisions (the agent OWNS — do not ask) from STRATEGIC/BUSINESS-REALITY decisions that only the user/org can answer and that DETERMINE SCOPE/RELEVANCE (ASK before investing). Migration strategy (brownfield vs greenfield), which systems/company-codes/domains are in scope, business priorities, chosen vendors/paths — these are org facts NOT derivable from code/data/sensible defaults. Assuming one risks wasting a whole research/build. A focused question is cheaper than discarded work.

rule: To decide whether a piece of SAP config that GENERATES output (DMEE tree node, smartform, routing) actually RENDERS/FIRES at runtime, the real generated OUTPUT is the arbiter — not the static config tables. DMEE_TREE_COND does NOT capture node-level deactivation, so reading only the condition gives false positives. If the artifact is replayable (e.g. ZSAPFPAYM_REPLAY for DMEE), generate it and read the real output BEFORE asserting a defect or alarming.
why: 2026-06-17 (DMEE structured-address forensics): I read DMEE_TREE_COND, saw node N_1531351640 condition still matched BR, and alarmed it duplicated the Dbtr PstlAdr (D-1). The real replayed BR XML showed ONE PstlAdr — node #1 was deactivated by a flag NOT in the condition table; the prior "D-1 resolved" was correct. Same session I also over-stated D-2 as a CBPR+ reject risk without checking the BR flow is DOMESTIC (no impact). The real output / the business context were the evidence, not the tree read.
how_to_apply: (1) Before claiming a DMEE/form node fires or suppresses, check for a deactivation/render flag OUTSIDE the condition table; if unsure, replay and read the real output. (2) Distinguish a DEAD-CONSTANT gate (e.g. UBISO=SE, a value that never occurs -> always suppresses = real bug) from a DYNAMIC exit-computed gate (e.g. -PstlAdr_More_Nodes overflow flag -> benign, emits for normal data). (3) Before asserting CBPR+/compliance reject risk, confirm the flow is cross-border SWIFT, not domestic local-clearing. (4) Update immediately and without defensiveness when real output contradicts a config-read claim.
cp_link_reason: Asserting runtime behavior from a config/condition read without the generated output is approximation without measuring; the real output IS the verifiable evidence.

rule: Knowledge discovered during a working conversation is NOT captured until it lives in a central store the next session auto-loads or can query (enhancement registry, claims.json, incidents.json, a domain doc, the capability_model, or feedback_rules.json). rule: When analyzing SAP RFC/BAPI traffic volume or patterns, ALWAYS apply the 2-axis method: (1) PROCESS axis from the FM name mapping to a business process, AND (2) ORIGIN axis from PARAMX host/dest/user identifying the satellite system. Neither axis alone is sufficient. A MuleSoft call and an internal report call to the same FM look identical without the ORIGIN axis. Coverage target: >90% of RFC volume explained.
why: Discovered s085: applying only 1 axis left 80.6% of external traffic unexplained or misattributed. The 2-axis engine explained 91.1% of business RFC volume. Without ORIGIN, MuleSoft's 1.62M calls would be labeled 'unknown internal'. CP-003 precision.
how_to_apply: Use process_mining/rfc_process_classifier.py (the engine). First classify by PARAM3 FM name -> process. Then enrich with PARAMX host/dest/user -> satellite/origin. Report as (process, origin) pairs. The 8.9% unexplained = known_unknowns, not a failure.

rule: When a tcode-based activity count for a domain is near zero, DO NOT conclude the process is inactive. The channel may be RFC/BAPI (invisible to tcode analysis). Always cross-validate with the RESULT side (CDHDR change documents, which are channel-agnostic -- every write is captured regardless of channel) before concluding a process runs at low volume.
why: Discovered s085: vendor master tcode count was ~0, suggesting MDM was idle. CDHDR showed KRED=143K change docs, dominantly dialog XK02 (M_AYIMBA 72K) + secondary ZBAPI_VENDOR_CHANGE (MP_ANCUTA 19K). The tcode-only view was a blind spot. CP-003: conclusion must be grounded in evidence from the correct source.
how_to_apply: Step 1: check rsau_audit_history SLGTC for the domain tcode. Step 2 if low: query cdhdr_history WHERE OBJECTCLAS = <relevant class> GROUP BY USERNAME, TCODE, YEAR(UDATE). Step 3: the TCODE column in CDHDR shows the channel (blank=RFC, populated=dialog). Cross-classify with rsau FM stream for the full picture.

rule: ALWAYS filter out JP_LOPEZ (and P_LUVHIMBI) RFC calls BEFORE reporting any RFC volume metrics from rsau_audit_history. Our own extraction is approximately 80-124K calls in a 4-month window (RFC_READ_TABLE 76K + DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET 3K + RFC_GET_FUNCTION_INTERFACE 1.5K + RSAU_API_* calls). Reporting without exclusion inflates the external-satellite share and overstates total traffic.
why: Discovered s085 when reconciling RFC volumes: JP_LOPEZ RFC_READ_TABLE alone = 76,137 calls in the analysis window. Including these in 'business RFC' or 'external traffic' metrics produces systematically wrong numbers. CP-003 precision: state your own footprint before quoting volumes.
how_to_apply: Add WHERE SLGUSER NOT IN ('JP_LOPEZ','P_LUVHIMBI') to all rsau_audit_history queries used for reporting satellite volumes. Document the exclusion in any claim that cites RFC volumes. The 80.6% external figure already has this exclusion applied.

rule: Before extracting any SAP object, RESOLVE the extraction and analysis method via the method registry (brain_v2/method_registry.json or process_mining/method_registry.py). Do NOT rediscover how to read a SAP object each session by trial-and-error (RFC_READ_TABLE -> fails -> hunt the FM -> probe interface -> build). The registry maps: DD02L.TABCLASS -> method (TRANSP=RFC_READ_TABLE ROWSKIPS-free; POOL=RFC key-only+FM; CLUSTER=FOR ALL ENTRIES; VIEW=RFC_READ_TABLE) plus element overrides (RSAU=RSAU_API_GET_LOG_DATA chunk<=6h; SM21/ST22/SNAP=/USE/BL_GET_SHORTDUMPS; SOAMANAGER=unresolvable). Cross-link: claim #241, D_DATA, retro knowledge/session_retros/retro_operating_model_method_2026-06-21.md.
why: Born 2026-06-21/22: every session we rediscovered extraction methods by trial (RFC_READ_TABLE -> fails -> hunt FM -> probe -> build). This is the #1 inefficiency identified in the operating-model retro. The registry is the fix: a resolver built from DD02L table class + hard-won element-specific overrides. Without it, a session wastes turns re-learning what RSAU requires chunked FM calls, what POOL tables return only keys, etc. Reference: process_mining/method_registry.py + brain_v2/method_registry.json (committed S-087).
how_to_apply:
1. python process_mining/method_registry.py <OBJECT_NAME> -- returns (extract_method, constraint, analyze_method, retention)
2. If the object is in the Gold DB already, check sqlite schema first -- may not need re-extraction
3. For unknown tables, check DD02L.TABCLASS via RFC_READ_TABLE to get the type, then apply the type rule
4. Never RFC_READ_TABLE a CLUSTER table (fails silently or errors) -- use FOR ALL ENTRIES
5. Never 2-day RSAU call -- chunk <=6h or connection hangs
6. The registry is EXTENSIBLE: when a new override is discovered, add it to OVERRIDE dict in method_registry.py and re-run to regenerate brain_v2/method_registry.json

rule: A claim with <2 independent evidence sources is WEAK. A single-source or surface-count finding is a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding. Before promoting any quantitative finding to a claim: (a) decode the detail (not just a count), (b) obtain a 2nd independent evidence source. Run the claims-health gate (brain_v2/claims_health.py) at session close to measure the STRONG/WEAK ratio. 21 WEAK TIER_1 claims are the current verification backlog (claim #242).
why: Born from claim #232 error (2026-06-21/22): 272 SM21 10054 resets -> concluded satellite connectivity failure (WRONG). The H74 chip decoded CENTDATA and found 269/272 = frontend GUI resets by end-user PCs, not satellite failures. The error was a surface count stated as a TIER_1 claim without a 2nd independent source. The claims-health gate (24.3% verification rate as of S-087) would have flagged #232 before it was stated. This generalizes the lesson: any finding derived from a single count/source must be treated as a hypothesis until corroborated. Cross-link: claim #242, superseded claim #232, brain_v2/claims_health.py.
how_to_apply:
1. python brain_v2/claims_health.py -- outputs STRONG/WEAK/UNSUPPORTED counts + weak_tier1_worklist
2. For any WEAK TIER_1 claim on the worklist: decode the detail (not just count rows) + get a 2nd independent source before citing it
3. A finding with only legacy_text or only empirical-count as evidence = WEAK -- add source_code or production_data corroboration
4. At session close: run claims_health.py and confirm STRONG count did not drop
5. Never state a quantitative claim as TIER_1 from a single surface count -- say TIER_2 (hypothesis) until a 2nd source confirms

rule: P01, D01, AND V01 RFC_READ_TABLE is wrapped by class SAIS which REJECTS ROWSKIPS with OPTION_NOT_VALID -- this is a LANDSCAPE-WIDE constraint, not a per-system quirk. This causes silent silent data truncation — not an error you see immediately. Use ROWCOUNT=0 with a tight WHERE partition (by FIKRS, date range, or other high-cardinality key) so each call stays manageable (there is NO ~60k platform ceiling: ROWCOUNT=0 returned 390,707 rows for BPGE in one call; partition is for memory/latency only). NEVER use ROWSKIPS-based pagination against P01/D01.
why: Session s088 (2026-06-22): refresh_funds_from_live.py used ROWSKIPS pagination against P01 and silently returned only 30,000 of 56,639 UNES funds — a 47% data loss with no error raised. The failure mode is silent: SAIS returns OPTION_NOT_VALID internally but the caller gets a partial result, not an exception. This also applies to D01 (reference_d01_rowskips_and_adt_ddic_limits.md, s081). The method_registry.json already records this constraint ('P01-secured: NO ROWSKIPS') but no behavioral rule captured the SILENT TRUNCATION risk and the correct partitioning pattern. | s093 (2026-06-29): D01 ROWSKIPS rejection confirmed DIRECTLY on FM tables (FMFINCODE, FMFINT) via gap-analysis script. rc=5 OPTION_NOT_VALID — identical to P01. Prior D01 reference (s081) was for ADT/DDIC context; this is the first FM-table direct confirmation on D01. | s-2026-07-02: V01 ROWSKIPS rejection confirmed DIRECTLY on USR02/PA0001/PA0105 (extract_v01_actor_grounding.py, rc=5 OPTION_NOT_VALID) -- 3rd system confirmed, closing the class: assume EVERY system in this landscape rejects ROWSKIPS unless proven otherwise (claim #319).
how_to_apply:
1. NEVER pass ROWSKIPS > 0 to RFC_READ_TABLE on P01 or D01. The call will appear to succeed with partial rows.
2. Instead: use ROWCOUNT=0 in a single call per partition. Partition by FIKRS for FM tables, by date range for event tables, by PSPID prefix for WBS.
3. Verify row counts against expected universe (e.g. compare with a COUNT(*) call or prior run): a result capped suspiciously near 30k means ROWSKIPS was used (no platform row ceiling exists for ROWCOUNT=0 — corrected s089).
4. For very large tables (hundreds of thousands of rows), partition by a secondary key (e.g. year, bukrs) for memory/latency — NOT because of a platform row ceiling.
5. Run `python process_mining/method_registry.py <TABLE>` to confirm the constraint before coding any extraction.
6. DEPRECATED: refresh_funds_from_live.py. Use scripts/extraction/p01_fm_ps_bcs_masterdata_refresh.py instead (claim #244).
correction_note_s089: S-089 correction: the ~60k ceiling was false. BPGE returned 390,707 rows, FMBH UNES 248,086 rows in single ROWCOUNT=0 calls (confirmed via _gold_sync_log 2026-06-22). The earlier truncation was caused by explicit ROWCOUNT=30000 in the deprecated script, not a platform limit. Rule text updated.
correction_note_s2026_07_02: Generalized to V01 (3rd confirmed system) 2026-07-02 during the unescrp actor-chain grounding extraction. Rule scope widened from P01+D01 to "this landscape" language; no behavior change, only evidence + wording.
correction_note_s2026_07_02b: Related quirk on the SAME wrapper found during the follow-up V01 Funds+WBS extraction (extract_v01_funds_wbs.py, claim #321): this SAIS-wrapped RFC_READ_TABLE also raises TABLE_WITHOUT_DATA (not FIELD_NOT_VALID) when a requested FIELDNAME does not exist on the table -- indistinguishable from a genuinely empty result. Confirmed: FMFINCODE has no FIVOR field, PRPS has no PSTRT field. ALWAYS validate the field list against DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET before concluding a table is empty on this landscape.

rule: When a bulk/delta extraction run completes without error, ALWAYS verify that the golden table row count approximately matches the P01 raw count for the same partition. A run that exits 0 CAN silently drop rows (e.g. via a key-collapse dedup on a table whose stored columns lack the full unique key). Do NOT dedup a line-item table unless the stored golden columns cover its FULL SAP unique key. For transaction tables (FMIOI, FMIFIIT, BSEG, etc.): check the DDIC key vs the golden column list before writing any dedup logic; if they differ, store ALL rows (no dedup) and use multiset-diff for delta.
why: S-089 (2026-06-22): gold_refresh.py txn-partitioned engine deduped by all-non-amount columns. FMIOI has 13 golden columns but its SAP unique key includes a line counter NOT in the golden extract. Result: 1,813,943 rows silently collapsed to 1,029,062 (~43% loss) with exit code 0. Only discovered via manual raw-count comparison: P01 UNES 2025 = 806,902 raw but golden had ~405k for ALL institutes (impossible). Fixed in commit 8190f3c. See claim #247.
how_to_apply: 1. After any extraction run: query P01 for COUNT(*) of the key partition and compare to golden row count. Allow <=0.1% variance for live churn (inserts/deletes between runs); >1% variance = re-investigate. 2. Before writing dedup logic for a table: run PRAGMA table_info(golden) to list golden cols, then check DD05L/DDIC key for the SAP table. If any key field is absent from the golden extract, do NOT dedup — store all rows. 3. For delta runs: use multiset diff (count occurrences of each full-row tuple) rather than set diff. 4. Verify FMIFIIT (ok: has FMBELNR+FMBUZEI+RLDNR+STUNR), BSEG (ok: BUKRS+BELNR+GJAHR+BUZEI), FMIOI (was broken: missing line counter in golden). 5. Add a post-pull assertion in the extractor: if n_total < 0.9 * expected_p01_count: HALT and report.

rule: Never re-derive AVC availability from FM document tables (FMIFIIT/BPJA/FMAVCT WRTTP arithmetic at posting-leaf level). The ONLY correct AVC figure comes from FMAVC_READ_TOTALS_FOR_ADDRESS (standard FM chain) or report FMAVCR. Leaf-level arithmetic produces 23.7% spurious negatives because the control object is DERIVED AND ROLLED-UP via strategy AFMA (OPF budget aggregated at TC, not at the posting commitment item). Hand-rolling silently misses the rollup and the negative-at-parent budget distribution.
why: committed_vs_available_detector.py was refuted empirically (s091): fund 196EAR4042 -> leaf arithmetic gave -$12.9M while V01 live FMAVC_READ_TOTALS_FOR_ADDRESS returned positive available. MBF fund: -$110M spurious negatives = 23.7% of active WBS. Root cause verified in ABAP source + config: strategy AFMA step 1 collapses all OPF commitment items to TC; leaf sum cannot reconstruct that rollup. This is the same class of error as GL balances from BSIS vs GLT0 (rule feedback_gl_balance_from_fs10n_not_bsis). Claims #253, #256, #259.
how_to_apply: 1. For any AVC availability question: call FMAVC_READ_TOTALS_FOR_ADDRESS via RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN on V01 or D01 (not P01 -- S_DEVELOP needed). Or run report FMAVCR in V01/D01. 2. To check-only AVC without commit (e.g. reservation pre-flight): FMFR_CREATE_FROM_DATA with I_FLG_CHECKONLY=X. 3. Never compute available = SUM(budget) - SUM(consumed) per (fund, fundsctr, cmmtitem) from fmavct or fmifiit -- that is WRONG because the control object is a derived address, not the posting leaf. 4. The Gold DB fmavct_* slice only has ALLOCTYPE_9=KBFC rows (consumption); it cannot reconstruct available on its own without the budget base from FMAVC_READ_TOTALS_FOR_ADDRESS. 5. If ALL FMAVC_* FMs are not RFC-enabled (TFDIR FMODE=empty): confirm S_DEVELOP on the calling user on V01/D01, use RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN wrapper pattern.

rule: When reconciling a fragment-assembled companion against its live HTML output, treat drift as BIDIRECTIONAL: (a) HTML-only blocks (present in the live companion but missing from fragments — port INTO the relevant fragment file); (b) fragment-only blocks (present in fragments but not yet rebuilt into the companion — DO NOT delete them; they merge correctly on the next rebuild). Never force byte-equality by discarding fragment-only content — that is an irreversible loss (CP-001). Reconciliation method: run --check → use difflib SequenceMatcher on newline-normalized lines → inspect BOTH insert-hunks (live-only) AND delete-hunks (fragment-only) → port on RAW bytes preserving CRLF+UTF-8 → verify no loss by diffing new built companion vs old → refresh MANIFEST baseline after confirming identity.
why: Session 2026-06-30 (commit 5bcb07a): the BCM Structured Address companion (companions/BCM_StructuredAddressChange.html) was ~21 KB short of the live companion. --check via build_bcm_structured_address_companion.py revealed three drift blocks: Block 1 = HTML-only CITI/CGI Dbtr+Cdtr analysis (+23,437 B across 181 lines) that existed in the live companion but never made it back into tabs/25_phase0.html; Block 2 = a missing leading emoji on a Phase 4 h3 in tabs/29_phase4.html; Block 3 = a fragment-only section (Citi test-tool 2026-06-26, brain claims #265/266/267) present in tabs/29_phase4.html but not in the companion because rebuild had never been re-run after that edit. The failure mode: a naive 'port everything from live to fragments' approach would have silently deleted Block 3 content. CP-001 requires treating every fragment-only hunk as intentional until confirmed redundant.
how_to_apply:
When --check reports a size/hash mismatch on a fragment-assembled companion:
1. Run the builder with --check to get difflib hunk output (or equivalent).
2. Classify each hunk: INSERT = live-only (missing from fragments); DELETE = fragment-only (missing from live).
3. INSERT hunks: identify the correct fragment file (by tab/section name) and port the raw bytes into it, preserving CRLF+UTF-8.
4. DELETE hunks: DO NOT remove them from fragments. Verify they are not already present elsewhere; if truly new, they will merge into the companion on rebuild.
5. Rebuild the companion and confirm the new live file matches the expected content.
6. Compare new vs old companion to verify no content loss in either direction.
7. Refresh the MANIFEST.json baseline (byte_count + sha256 + sha256_lf) ONLY after confirming byte-identical integrity.
8. Never update the MANIFEST baseline to the pre-reconciliation state — only update after the full reconciliation is clean.
cp_link_reason: CP-001 'Knowledge over velocity': the fragment-only content represents work already done (brain claims #265/266/267 analysis) that would be irreversibly deleted if the reconciler only read one direction of the diff. Velocity would suggest 'just make the fragments match the live companion'; CP-001 demands inspecting what the live companion is missing too. The bidirectional check is the minimum-loss path.

rule: Before loading budget (or any master/transactional value) into a target system, READ the target's existing state at that EXACT key first -- an idempotency check, not just a presence check. If a value already exists at that key, NET-CHECK before posting (do not just add a new line), because most SAP posting APIs (e.g. BAPI_0050_CREATE for BCS budget) are additive, not upsert -- posting again at an already-populated key creates a double, not a correction.
why: Session 2026-07-06: 14 cost-recovery funds were loaded into V01 without first reading V01's existing state at the target (fund, fund center, commitment item) key. V01 already had budget at CI-11/13 for 11 of the 14 funds, so the new ENTR/B1 posts doubled the budget rather than establishing it. Compounded by an earlier mis-addressing in the same session (loading at commitment item TC, then at fund center HEQ, both wrong for this batch per claim #338) -- three separate write-without-verify-first mistakes on the same batch. Reversal was blocked (reversal reasons not active for FY2026 in both D01 and V01, claim #324), forcing a negative-offset BAPI_0050_CREATE workaround (claim #325) to net the doubles/mis-addresses back to zero -- extra cleanup work that a pre-write read would have avoided entirely.
how_to_apply:
1. Identify the EXACT key the write targets (for BCS: fund + fund center/FISTL + commitment item + fiscal year + ledger/version -- not just the fund).
2. Read the target system's live state (FMBL/FMAVCT for budget; the equivalent master/transaction table for any other domain) at that exact key BEFORE posting anything.
3. If a value already exists at that key: NET-CHECK (compare the source value against what's already there) -- do not blindly add. If the API is additive (most BAPI_0050_* budget posts are), compute the delta needed and post only the delta (or the negative-offset if you already over-posted).
4. Never assume a target starts empty just because the source system has the value -- targets used for prior testing/dev work commonly already carry partial or full state.
5. This generalizes the 'verify before alarming / verify by re-read' family (feedback_verify_before_alarming_and_update_on_correction) to the WRITE side: verify BEFORE you write, not just before you report.
cp_link_reason: CP-003 'Precision, evidence, facts': writing to a target system without first reading its current state at the exact key is an unverified assumption (the target is empty / the target matches the source), not a checked fact. The fix is the same discipline CP-003 already demands for claims -- verify before asserting -- applied to the write path instead of the report path.

rule: Audit parallel worktree branches at session start AND close. A commit that lives only on a `.claude/worktrees/<name>` branch is invisible to `git status`/`git log` on your own branch and is NO safer than uncommitted work -- gone if the disk dies. Durability = the work is on ORIGIN, not merely 'committed'.
why: Session 2026-07-07: the worktree branch `unruffled-williamson-810b11` @5285e92 held the entire AVC recurring-pipeline layer -- 5 claims, gold_table_registry +266 rows, a capability-model bump, and the new 330-line scripts/extraction/psm_avc_refresh.py -- committed but never merged or pushed. Nothing on the active feature branch or origin referenced it; it was one disk failure from total loss. This is the concrete mechanism behind the measured weakest capability, DURABILITY (0.233): 'I committed' felt safe but the work was stranded locally.
how_to_apply:
1. At session start and close run: `git worktree list`; for each worktree HEAD `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> HEAD || echo STRANDED`; and `git log --oneline origin/<branch>..HEAD | wc -l` for unpushed on the current branch.
2. Any tip NOT an ancestor of a pushed branch = stranded knowledge -> merge it, preserve-first (union; on a claim/record id collision, keep the earlier-referenced side's ids and RENUMBER the other, then fix its citations -- both branches took claim ids 304-308 here, AVC renumbered to 341-345).
3. Never treat a local commit as durable. Push before you consider the work captured.
4. Prune only fully-merged worktrees, and only when no parallel session is using one (no active-work.md lease).
cp_link_reason: CP-002 'Preserve first, context is cheap': stranded local commits are the failure mode where hard-won knowledge is silently at risk of irreversible loss. Preserving it means making it durable (on origin) and merging without clobbering, not just leaving it 'committed somewhere'.

rule: Before answering ANY scope question -- which SAP modules/components exist, what is actually used, how UNESCO operates, what the integrations are -- READ brain_v2/system_profile/unesco_system_profile.json (it is rendered at the top of BRAIN_INDEX.md at bootstrap). NEVER re-derive the footprint from cvers/audit logs inside a conversation. Always separate INSTALLED vs CONFIGURED vs PRODUCTIVE.
why: s097 (2026-07-28): an external Business-Process-Review questionnaire was answered by re-deriving the footprint live. RE-FX, SD, FI-AA, PM and TRM were all reported as 'not implemented / not evidenced' -- all five are PRODUCTIVE (RE-FX alone: 312 contracts, 1,600 rental objects, 6 custom packages). An entire category was missing: third-party add-ons (EPI-USE Labs on HCM, ACL Data Link extracting daily, Winshuttle installed-dormant) -- two of which are independent DATA-EXIT channels, i.e. directly material to a data-governance answer. Root cause: executed_objects_domain_map has no bucket for RE-FX nor for /EPIUSE/, /ACLDL/, /WINSHTLQ/, /GBX01/, so 40% of execution volume sits in 'Uncatalogued' -- and absence-in-the-map was read as absence-in-the-system. The user had to catch the same class of error twice in one session.
how_to_apply: 1) Read the profile FIRST; it is the base fact-sheet of the tenant. 2) If the profile lacks the answer, probe P01 read-only and WRITE THE RESULT BACK into the profile -- never leave a new fact in the chat. 3) Never infer 'not implemented' from absence in executed_objects_domain_map or from a table missing in the Gold DB: both are FLOORS, not inventories. Say 'not evidenced -- to confirm' and probe. 4) State INSTALLED vs CONFIGURED vs PRODUCTIVE explicitly; 177 components are installed and most ship by default.

rule: When you find a defect in a declared fact — a wrong path, a wrong label, a wrong denominator, a stale binding — do NOT fix the value and move on. Do TWO things first: (1) SWEEP for siblings across every store, because the same hand wrote the same mistake elsewhere; (2) if it appears TWICE, it is structural — write the GATE, not the second correction. And when the defect lives inside main() where no check can reach it, EXTRACT THE DECISION TO A PURE FUNCTION FIRST: inline logic cannot be gated, so it fails by being read rather than by being checked.
why: s097: C3 was published as PROPOSED — an idea with no code — while its tool ran, because ONE prose entry sat in a list of paths. Correcting it would have looked like a fix. The sweep found the SAME prose copied into a second store. Nothing had ever checked whether a path field held a path. Separately, the drift algorithm's two real defects (raw monthly volumes over unequal months -> 11 false signals; z-scores on a 2-month baseline -> z=1016) were BOTH found by reading output, never by a check, because the statistic lived inside main(). A field or a decision that nothing can check does not fail loudly — it makes everything built on it SILENTLY WRONG, which is worse than a gap, because a gap is visible.
how_to_apply: 1. grep the defective SHAPE across all stores before fixing the instance. 2. count the sightings: one = fix; two = gate. 3. to gate a decision buried in main(), extract it to a pure function with its inputs explicit, have main() call it, then write the cases — one case per defect that ALREADY happened, phrased so a failure reads as 'the old defect is back'. 4. register the gate as a method and wire it into rebuild_all + the analysis cycle; a gate nobody runs is documentation.
evidence: brain_v2/methods/validate_paths.py (149 path fields, 5 stores, rebuild 0a3) · process_mining/detect_drift.py departures_for() · Zagentexecution/mcp-backend-server-python/rfc_helpers.py plan_field_chunks() · golden cases 43->63 · claim #385

rule: A trigger reports EVIDENCE and the KIND of response required — CYCLE, EXTRACTION or AUTHORING. It must NEVER name a script to run. The knowledge of WHAT to run and IN WHICH ORDER lives in one place, the analysis cycle, so adding an algorithm means PLACING IT IN THE CHAIN — never remembering to call it. The same holds for a new capability: it is not delivered until it sits in the orchestration at its correct dependency position.
why: naming a script inside a trigger is a decision taken on demand, and on-demand decisions are exactly the ones that stop being taken — which is the hole the trigger file exists to close, so committing it there is self-defeating. It also scatters the ordering knowledge across ten call sites, where it silently rots: nine of the ten triggers named individual scripts and none of them knew that write-path attribution must precede boundary discovery.
how_to_apply: 1. new algorithm => place it in run_analysis_cycle.py at its dependency level, and say WHY that level. 2. new trigger => it fires on a measured change and declares needs=CYCLE|EXTRACTION|AUTHORING. 3. if the answer is 'run X', the real answer is 'X belongs in the cycle'. 4. EXTRACTION stays outside the cycle on purpose — it depends on a connection and on a human deciding it is time.
evidence: brain_v2/methods/run_analysis_cycle.py (A8 placed at L2 because its INTERFACE channel names the functions the satellite derivation groups on) · brain_v2/methods/check_triggers.py (RESPONSE table; 9 triggers converted)

rule: An analysis written up as PROSE is not knowledge the system can use. Prose IDENTIFIES what to look for; a measurement CONFIRMS it. Never let a documented fact stand as evidence on its own, and never let it sit in the same field as a derived one — keep DECLARED and DERIVED separate and emit a VERDICT: CONFIRMED (both agree), UNCONFIRMED PROSE (documented, not visible in the data), UNDECLARED (visible in the data, not documented).
why: prose that is never structured gets RE-DERIVED by the next question, and the two answers then drift with nothing able to notice. Measured instance: the integration map classified every flow into 8 channels — RFC, IDoc, middleware, file jobs, batch input, LSMW, DBCON, HTTP/SOAP — including that Coupa arrives as a FILE processed by a job, and that TULIP/UNESDIR come over DBCON and fail 93% of the time. All in markdown tables. So `interface_boundary.json` (F1) contained the string 'channel' ZERO times, and algorithm A8 was about to re-derive the whole taxonomy from the audit log while the answer sat in a document nobody could query. Worse, the first cross-check APPENDED the declared channel next to the derived ones, which silently promotes a sentence in a table to the standing of a measurement and destroys the comparison that makes either one useful.
how_to_apply: 1. when an analysis produces a classification, emit a STRUCTURED store, not only a document — the document explains, the store is queried. 2. before deriving something, check whether it was already analysed and left as prose. 3. keep declared and derived in SEPARATE fields with an explicit verdict. 4. a disagreement is a FINDING on one side or the other — stale documentation, a stopped flow, or a blind derivation — and until both sides exist you cannot even have the disagreement.
evidence: brain_v2/build_channel_registry.py -> integration_channels.json (48 flows, 8 channels, 30 artifacts) parsed from knowledge/domains/Integration/integration_map_complete.md · process_mining/attribute_changes_to_programs.py resolve_channels() verdict
superseded_why: same finding, written twice in one session by two passes over the same conversation. The surviving rule is the more precise one: it names the documented finding a HYPOTHESIS TO VERIFY and carries three verdicts including CONTRADICTED, which this one collapsed into a single 'unconfirmed'. Kept rather than deleted so the duplication itself stays visible — it is evidence that a promotion pass can run twice and not notice.

rule: A check must never be able to switch itself off quietly. Any guard that can be SKIPPED — an optional import, a missing file, an absent table, an exception path — must record the skip as a FAILURE or at minimum print it. `except ImportError: x = None` inside a test harness is forbidden.
why: measured this session: the golden cases for algorithm A8 ran for a whole session against a function that no longer existed. A rename turned `_channel` into `resolve_channels`, the import raised, the bare `except ImportError` swallowed it, six cases stopped executing and the harness printed OK. The count went 69 -> 68 and nothing flagged it — the only reason it was caught is that the total was read against memory of the previous run. A gate reporting success while not running is worse than no gate, because a missing gate is visible and a silent one is trusted. The same shape appeared in check_triggers.py, where an `except sqlite3.Error: pass` made a new measurement return None and read as 'nothing to measure'.
how_to_apply: 1. in a harness, an unavailable dependency appends to `failures`, never sets a flag to None silently. 2. in a measurement, a caught exception PRINTS what could not be measured. 3. when a check's own case count drops, treat it as a defect until proven otherwise — the count is the gate on the gate. 4. never rename a function without running the harness that imports it.
evidence: brain_v2/methods/validate_algorithms.py (5 ImportError paths now append to failures; 68 -> 74 cases once they ran again) · brain_v2/methods/check_triggers.py (sqlite3.Error now prints)

rule: A documented finding is a HYPOTHESIS TO VERIFY, never evidence to add. Use the prose to IDENTIFY what to look for, then CONFIRM it against derived data, and report the verdict — CONFIRMED, CONTRADICTED or UNVERIFIED. Never merge a documented claim into a derived result set: that launders a document into a measurement and makes the two impossible to separate afterwards. And before deriving anything, CHECK WHETHER IT WAS ALREADY ANALYSED: an analysis that never became structured gets silently re-derived.
why: s097, twice in one hour. FIRST: the write-channel taxonomy — RFC, IDoc, middleware, FILE, batch input, LSMW, DBCON, HTTP/SOAP — was fully analysed and written into `integration_map_complete.md` as MARKDOWN TABLES. The consequence was measurable: `interface_boundary.json` contains the string 'channel' ZERO times, and algorithm A8 was about to re-derive the same taxonomy from the audit log while the answer sat in a document nobody could query. Two answers to the same question, drifting apart, with no way to notice. SECOND: on wiring the registry in, the first version APPENDED the declared channel to the derived list with confidence 0.9 — prose dressed as measurement. The user's correction was exact: 'mira la prosa para identificar, pero debes confirmarlo con A8. Prosa sola no vale de nada.'
how_to_apply: 1. before deriving, grep knowledge/ for the same question — it may already be answered in prose. 2. if it is, PARSE it into a store keyed on something an algorithm holds, do not re-analyse it. 3. keep the two SEPARATE: declared in one field, derived in another, plus an explicit verdict. 4. treat CONTRADICTED as the valuable output — it means the documentation and the system disagree, which could not even be expressed before. MECHANIZED as M16: `brain_v2/methods/audit_prose_classifications.py` measures how much classification is still trapped — 59 in the LIVE reference, 26 already structured, 34 historical. A document whose table is genuinely illustrative declares itself with `<!-- narrative-only -->`; the point is that the choice becomes DELIBERATE. The worked example of clearing one is `brain_v2/build_channel_registry.py`. NOTE on the measurement itself: the first count reported 87 by including session retros and plans — technically derived and practically useless, which is its own kind of wrong answer.
evidence: brain_v2/build_channel_registry.py -> integration_channels.json (48 flows, 8 channels, 30 artifacts) · check_declared() in process_mining/attribute_changes_to_programs.py

rule: When you are told an entity exists, SEARCH FOR THAT NAME. Never substitute a naming convention for the search. 'Is there anything custom?' answered with LIKE 'Z%' OR 'Y%' is not the same question and can return the opposite answer.
why: s097. Asked to verify four declared web-service integrations, I tested WSNAME LIKE 'Z%' OR 'Y%', got zero, and reported 'there are NO custom web services in P01' — a confident finding that contradicted the integration map. Two things were wrong. The four declared names (BOC_INVOICE_WF, CSI_AWS_EC2, CSI_AWS_S3, UNJSPF_INTERFACE1) do not start with Z or Y, so the filter could never have found them. And the SAME filter erased the LIVE SuccessFactors channel: eight inbound services (EMPLOYEEMASTERDATABUNDLEREPLIC, POSITIONREPLICATIONREQUEST_IN and six more) authored by named people, carrying no custom prefix because they are SAP-DELIVERED DEFINITIONS THAT WERE ACTIVATED. A prefix says who SHIPPED an object, never whether it is USED here. The user caught it with 'esto me parece que esta mal.'
how_to_apply: 1. take the names you were given and look them up, one by one. 2. only then widen with a pattern, and report the two results separately. 3. never let a prefix stand for 'custom', 'used' or 'ours' — SAP-delivered objects that are activated are part of the AS-RUN system. 4. a negative result from a pattern is not evidence of absence.
evidence: claim #396 supersedes #395; wsheader AUTHOR<>'SAP' = 8 SuccessFactors services; icfservice Z%/Y% = 304 — both invisible under the first test

rule: D01 CODE IS FOR DEVELOPING. WHEN YOU EVALUATE, READ THE CODE FROM P01 — because the code may never have reached P01. Any statement about how the system BEHAVES must be anchored in production source. D01 answers 'what have we built'; only P01 answers 'what is valid'.
why: s097, measured. Package ZPBC holds 114 objects in D01 and 77 in P01 — 37 never reached production, INCLUDING SIXTEEN TRANSACTIONS and 3 BAdI implementations. A conclusion drawn from the D01 inventory would have overstated the production footprint by 32%, and would have described transactions no user can run. The user stated it exactly: 'Codigo de D01 es cuando desarrollamos. Cuando evaluamos es de P01, ya que puede ser que el codigo nunca haya llegado a P01.'
how_to_apply: 1. P01 source IS readable, read-only, via RPY_PROGRAM_READ — no ADT and no write path involved. Reading what is active is how you CHECK a claim instead of assuming it. 2. Classes need the pool: <CLASSNAME> padded to 30 with '=' then 'CP', whose include list carries one CM<xx> include per method. The pool ALONE is ~25 lines of skeleton — reporting that as the class makes a 1,296-line implementation look empty. 3. Keep the two corpora SEPARATE (extracted_sap_p01/ vs the D01 corpus). Merging them destroys the only distinction that matters: deployed versus merely existing. 4. When they differ, the DIFFERENCE is a finding — unreleased work, abandoned work, or dev-only tooling, and each means something different.
evidence: Zagentexecution/sap_data_extraction/scripts/extract_p01_source.py; ZPBC D01 114 vs P01 77; ZCL_IM__UNESCO_ENCUMB 1,296 lines read from production; claims #397, #398

rule: Anything scheduled must RECORD THAT IT RAN, and something must READ that record and act. A schedule alone is not a mechanism: a task that stops firing produces no error and no artifact, and the absence of fresh output reads as 'nothing changed'.
why: s097. The analysis cycle was built to close the 'on demand means never' hole, then sat unscheduled for a whole session — the same hole, one level up. Scheduling it is only half: a missed week is SILENT unless the loop can see its own gap. The user framed the requirement exactly: 'si detectas que no fue corrida durante la semana, hazlo una vez que lo detectes' — detect AND act, not detect.
how_to_apply: 1. the scheduled thing writes a state file with its last run, step count and failures. 2. the trigger evaluation MEASURES the gap and fires a response class. 3. the SESSION START surfaces it, because a measurement nobody reads changes nothing and session start is the one moment the agent is guaranteed to look. 4. report FAILED STEPS too: a cycle that ran and failed half its steps is worse than one that did not run, because its artifacts look fresh.
evidence: brain_v2/methods/cycle_state.json; check_triggers CYCLE_STALE_DAYS=8; cycle_headline() in brain_v2/session_start_hook.py; three Windows tasks in Ready state

rule: A string replace that does not match FAILS SILENTLY and leaves the file half-edited. Never patch a file with an unverified `s.replace(...)` and move on. Either use an ANCHORED edit that errors when the anchor is missing, or assert the change landed before continuing — `assert new in s`, or re-read the file. AND THE WORSE SIBLING: an escape that survives the heredoc as a CONTROL CHARACTER. Writing a regex through a heredoc turned every intended \b into a literal U+0008 backspace inside a RAW string, so the pattern compiled cleanly and matched nothing anywhere.
why: s097, FOUR times in one session. A call site was left pointing at a renamed function; a print block kept referencing a field that no longer existed; a signature changed on one side only; and the run-recording block never entered the cycle at all — I only noticed because the state file did not appear. The common cause is a non-ASCII character in the match text: the middle dot in 'ran · failed' did not match through a heredoc, so the replace returned the string unchanged and the script reported success. THE SCRIPT SAID IT WORKED. Each of these cost a full re-run, and one shipped a broken file to a background job that then failed on its own. || s097, the same root with a different symptom and it cost far more: _numbers_in_prose() returned 0 across 3,544 long-string leaves in 92 stores. I retyped the 'identical' line outside the module, it worked, and I concluded the bug was scope or shadowing — because retyping produced a real two-character escape while the file held control bytes. I marked the checker BROKEN and moved on. The actual fix was one line. THE TELL: when a regex matches NOTHING ANYWHERE, doubt the PATTERN BYTES before the logic — `git diff | cat -A` shows them, reasoning does not.
how_to_apply: 1. anchored edits by preference — a missing anchor must ERROR, not no-op. 2. if you must use replace, ASSERT the result changed: `assert s != before` per hunk, not once at the end. 3. never put non-ASCII in a match string; anchor on ASCII-only lines. 4. after patching, RUN the thing — syntax-checking is not enough, a silent no-op parses perfectly. 5. patching the same file in several fragments compounds this: read it whole first. 6. never write a regex or an escape-bearing literal through a heredoc — use the editor. 7. a pattern matching nothing anywhere is a corrupted literal until proven otherwise: hexdump it. 8. when you write a docstring ABOUT an escape, remember the docstring is not raw either.
evidence: s097: resolve_channels signature, channel_evidence print, cycle_state write block || NUM regex in audit_prose_classifications.py

rule: The bootstrap index is GENERATED from the stores, never written — and it must carry the SHAPE of the installation, not only its inventory: the process spine ranked by domains served, the cross-cutting topics that are NOT domains, and the measured maturity. One read must give the PROFILE, including what CANNOT be seen.
why: s097. The index listed modules, layers and counts — an inventory — and a session could read all of it and still not know that this tenant exists to run BUDGET-TO-REPORT, that SECURITY is a column and not a domain so searching for it returns nothing, or that 80% of traffic is external so any answer assuming people in screens is wrong before it starts. That is SHAPE, and shape is what makes an inventory usable. Ranking B2R first because SIX domains serve it — measured, not asserted — also means the order corrects itself if the installation changes.
how_to_apply: 1. every block DERIVED from a store; if it cannot be derived it does not belong in the index. 2. rank by measurement, never by opinion. 3. name what CANNOT be seen — a session that does not know the blind spot reads absence as evidence. 4. cross-cutting topics get their own section precisely BECAUSE they are not domains: if the only way to find security is to already know it is column E, the index has failed.
evidence: brain_v2/build_brain_index.py: _process_spine, _security_block, _integration_block, _maturity_block; index 4.0KB -> 9.6KB, all generated

rule: A capability column that is asked N times and OWNED BY NOBODY stays empty in every row. When a column is systemically empty, the first hypothesis is NOT neglect — it is that the topic has no SUBJECT: no store, no composer, no place where the answer accumulates. Give it a cross-cutting subject and the column fills; keep treating it as N independent gaps and it never will.
why: s097, TWO instances in one session and they behave identically. E_AUTH was empty in 16 of 21 domains and searching the domain list for 'security' returned nothing — it was a column with no subject. R_S4_READINESS was empty in 21 of 21, the only COMPLETELY empty column, and it had a sub-scorecard nobody owned. Both filled the moment they got a store, a composer and a section in the bootstrap index. The corollary bites too: because the S/4 sub-scorecard held only SIX TECHNICAL factors, a COMMERCIAL exposure (digital access / API cost — arguably the largest for an 80%-external tenant) had nowhere to land and simply was not recorded. A subject shapes what can be seen, so an incomplete subject is a blind spot with a structure.
how_to_apply: 1. a systemically empty column => ask WHO OWNS IT before asking who neglected it. 2. build the subject as a store composed of components, each saying what it needs and whether we hold it — never an empty section, because an empty security or readiness report reads as GOOD NEWS. 3. give it a section in the bootstrap index: if the only way to find a topic is to already know which column it is, the index has failed. 4. check the subject's own factor list for a MISSING KIND — technical factors only usually means a commercial or organisational dimension is invisible.
evidence: brain_v2/build_security_posture.py (E_AUTH) and brain_v2/build_s4_readiness.py (R_S4_READINESS, 21 of 21 empty, 6 technical factors + 1 commercial added); claims #404 #406 #407

rule: Measure the system against WHAT IT DOES TODAY, not against what a design document once specified. A design doc is archaeology and vocabulary; it is not a conformance target unless someone still intends it. Before treating any as-designed statement as a yardstick, ASK WHETHER IT WAS SUPERSEDED — and go looking for the current-state research FIRST, because it is usually harder to find than the blueprints and always worth more.
why: s097. I ingested five 2017 blueprints and produced 17 conformance rules whose verdicts were mostly NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Every measurement was real. The FRAME was wrong: UNESCO kept SAP as the system of RECORD and deliberately moved the system of ENGAGEMENT outside it, so 'the blueprint specified X and X does not exist' describes a design that became irrelevant, not a system that failed. The peer project's own current-state research had ALREADY NAMED this failure mode — it re-scored one of its claims as 'a DESIGN-DOC ARTIFACT OVERTAKEN BY THE AS-RUN' and deprecated any dialog-based baseline with 'a redesign baselined on dialog usage is baselined on <20% of the real traffic'. I walked into the trap their document describes, because sources/2017_design/ was easier to find than knowledge/36 and knowledge/37.
how_to_apply: 1. look for the AS-RUN research before the design corpus — filenames like 'asrun', 'e2e', 'current', 'operating model' beat 'BBP' and 'design'. 2. when a design statement fails against data, the FIRST hypothesis is that it was superseded, not that the system is broken. 3. a NOT_IMPLEMENTED verdict needs a second question: does anyone still intend it? If not, it is history. 4. keep what a blueprint is genuinely good for — VOCABULARY. The AVC address triple named a distinction we had measured and had no word for, and that survives the reframe. 5. the real yardstick is the measured end-to-end: here, human validation at ~21 days against an integration seam of 1.8 days says the leverage is human throughput, which no blueprint comparison would have shown.
evidence: claim superseding the framing of #409/410/414/415; unesco-sap-brain/knowledge/36_asrun_operating_model_reeval.md and 37_workplan_e2e_integrated.md

rule: When a join/lookup between two tables returns nothing, compare the FIELD WIDTHS of the two key columns (DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET) before extracting any more tables chasing the link. A join between two differently-sized keys sharing the same field NAME cannot ever succeed, no matter how many more tables are pulled.
why: s098, A16_payroll_end_to_end. Three separate extractions chased the payroll symbolic-account-to-GL-account link through T030/T030B/T52EZ before a single DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET call ended the line of enquiry: T030-KTOSL (the FI account-determination transaction key) is CHAR(3); a payroll symbolic account (T52EK-SYMKO) is CHAR(4). Two different keys wearing the same field name — no join could ever have worked. The cost was three extractions instead of one field-metadata call.
how_to_apply: 1. The moment a join/lookup against a candidate key returns zero or nonsensical results, STOP extracting more candidate tables. 2. Call DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET (or read the DDIC) on BOTH sides of the join and compare LENG. 3. If the widths differ, the fields are NOT the same key regardless of the shared name — go find the real bridge (often a customer-range table, see feedback about T9POST) or read the POSTED DOCUMENTS instead of the configuration (companion rule). 4. Record the field-width fact in algorithm_memory so no other algorithm repeats the same trap.
evidence: brain_v2/methods/algorithm_memory.json subject '_field_width'; claims #463/#464; brain_v2/payroll_discovery.json .resolved_posting._why_config_search_fails

rule: When the configuration tables will not yield an assignment (a derivation, an account determination, a routing decision), read the POSTED DOCUMENTS instead — the resolved result sits on one row there, and the cardinality measured IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (forward and back) identifies where the decision is actually made.
why: s098, A16_payroll_end_to_end part 7 ('the resolved posting'). The payroll account determination defeated a configuration search for a structural reason (see feedback_compare_field_widths_before_more_extraction). PPDIT — the posting document ITEMS — carries the FI transaction key and the resolved GL account together on one row. Over a 4,000-row sample: 2 of 4 keys fan out to several GL accounts, while 28 of 28 GL accounts belong to exactly one key. One-to-many forward, one-to-one back — which is what proved the account is decided BEYOND the key (by the wage type), a reading no configuration table could have given directly.
how_to_apply: 1.
